articleTitle: Reference Signal Generation for a Unified Power Quality Conditioner in Urban Passenger Heavy Rail Electrification System
abstract: This paper presents the reference signal generation for the unified power quality conditioner (UPQC) in urban passenger heavy rail electrification systems. This study focuses on performance evaluation of power quality improvement in the dynamic passenger load condition. The unit vector generator template (UVGT) and the indirect detection based on instantaneous power theory (PQ) are utilized to generate the reference signals for the UPQC. The simulation results confirm that the reference signal generation based on the proposed method can provide good performance. The harmonic current mitigation, power factor improvement, voltage sagswell compensations can be achieved efficiently by the proposed method. The power quality improvement performance metrics are aligned with the IEEE Standard 519.

articleTitle: Smart Solar Energy Tracking and Forecasting System Using Data Analytics and LSTM Models
abstract: This paper presents a solar energy analysis system that utilizes data analytics for enhanced performance. The system integrates solar panel tracking technology, real-time data visualization through Power BI, and forecasting using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) techniques and regression analysis. The accuracy of the solar tracking system was evaluated using root mean square error (RMSE = 6.05) and mean squared error (MSE = 7.45). To further assess the forecasting model, the study examines the impact of error margins on practical applications. Additionally, scalability considerations for larger solar farms and potential forecasting limitations, such as environmental factors and long-term accuracy, are discussed.

articleTitle: Stroke Classification from Facial Features Using Machine Learning
abstract: Face represents the important features for the visual assessment of the stroke patient. The facial stroke is known as the inability to move a part, one side, or both sides of the facial muscle from nerve damage. However, stroke and bell's palsy are similar symptoms on the patient's face that are difficult to diagnose. Therefore, this research will propose an efficient machine learning algorithm for facial stroke classification. Our research gathers the imaging data from the two published dataset that consist of the facial stroke images from facial droop and facial paralysis and the facial normal images from facial expression. This dataset selects the smile expression to extract the face features by using the facial mapping landmark method. These landmarks are used to calculate the facial features for training the machine learning algorithms that consist of the support vector machine, k-nearest neighbor, decision tree, random forest, logistic regression, AdaBoost, and Bayesian Classifier methods. These methods were trained by using the training accuracy and evaluated by using the accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. From the experimental results, the random forest represents the most accurate percentage of training and testing measurements. Therefore, this research proposes the random forest algorithm to be the efficient algorithm to classify the facial stroke from face features of smile expression.

articleTitle: Study on Damage to Flexible Pavement Road in Thailand: Identification Types of Crack on Roads Using Image Processing Takes
abstract: The detection and identification of flexible pavement road cracks pose a significant challenge for civil engineers when they start work at the beginning level, as it requires extensive work experience of engineers in classifying types of cracks for planning road maintenance. Inaccurate analysis and identification of cracks can negatively affect the quality of maintenance work and threaten the safety of road users in the future. This paper presents a case study of 60 asphalt roads managed by the Provincial Administrative Organization (PAO) in central of Thailand (case of two provinces, Uthai Thani and Nakhon Sawan), focusing on identification type road cracks. The study aims to address issues related to data preparation and classification across various domains Our data are fed model, which is photography to medium-resolution images of flexible pavement road cracks so that guidelines for engineers' inspection and identification of road cracks. We propose the development of a U-Net model specifically designed for image processing tasks. The results indicate that the U-Net model is effective in converting road cracks images into segmentation masks, and this effectiveness is evaluated using four well-defined key performance indicators.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of Energy Consumption in an Electric ATV Agricultural Robot Under Varying Loads and Terrain Conditions
abstract: Under current environmental conditions, traditional agriculture often faces significant problems such as labor shortages, unstable crop yields, and inappropriate and wasteful resource use. Robotic technology is an alternative and rationale for automating work to increase its accuracy. Agricultural robots are set to play a key role in modern agriculture, which requires significant increases in efficiency, precision, energy, and environmental sustainability. However, another important problem in driving robots to work efficiently is effectively planning energy use to plan work and reduce costs. Agricultural robots that move to carry heavy objects require much energy. Suppose there is a mathematical model that helps calculate energy use under different load conditions and work areas. In that case, it will allow robots to manage the time to charge energy and work efficiently. From the simple energy consumption modeling experiment using the data of the movement speed and the robot parameters such as weight and gear ratio and comparing with the actual energy measurement from the battery, The trend of energy consumption compared to the horizontal movement condition tends in the same direction. The electrical energy supplied to the system was found to be higher than the energy used in the movement calculated from the model. Reasonable regarding the efficiency of the motor and drive units in the specified straight-line condition with an estimated value of 60% and in the specified incline at approximately 25%.

articleTitle: 3D Reconstruction of Steel Rail using Multi-view Cameras and Mask R-CNN
abstract: This study proposed a method that integrates multi-view image processing, depth estimation, and point cloud generation to accurately reconstruct a 3D model of a rail. The method is tested by positioning two webcams on the left and right sides of the rail and capturing three images of the entire rail. These images are combined into a panorama using image stitching techniques. Depth estimation is then performed using Monocular Depth Estimation, followed by background separation using Mask R-CNN to isolate the rail. The 3D model is reconstructed through 3D Reconstruction, and its quality is evaluated using an accuracy assessment. The resulting 3D model of the rail demonstrated an accuracy of 84.56% when compared to the ground truth, with the rail head 99.87%, the rail web 65.67%, and the rail foot 72.66%.

articleTitle: Automatic Alzheimer Screening on Clock Drawing Test Using Deep Learning : ASDL
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease is a progressive neurological condition that impairs memory, cognitive abilities, and daily functioning, making early detection critical for effective intervention. The Clock Drawing Test (CDT) is commonly used to screening between Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and healthy control (HC) cases. However, traditional scoring methods rely heavily on subjective expert judgment, which introduces bias and variability. To address these issues, this research explores an automated deep learning-based approach for analyzing CDT images. We compare the performance of four state-of-the-art Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models—DenseNet, ResNet, EfficientNet, and Vision Transformer (ViT)—for classifying Alzheimer’s severity using a collected dataset of CDT images. From the experimental results, DenseNet-121 outperformed the other models, achieving a training accuracy of 99.95% and a validation accuracy of 98.84%. Moreover, this model demonstrated strong performance in testing, as measured by precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrix. The model also revealed significant detection areas, focusing on the clock’s center and the direction of its hands, using Score-CAM interpretation. This research proposes DenseNet-121 as an effective tool for analyzing CDT images, contributing to early detection of Alzheimer’s disease in healthcare applications.

articleTitle: Selective Harmonic Elimination in Single Phase Inverter with LC Filter using Artificial Neural Network
abstract: In this paper presents the using of selective harmonic elimination pulse width modulation (SHEPWM) switching technique in the unipolar single phase inverter with LC type of filter circuit and concept of using artificial neural network (ANN) to simplify the designs of components value to the result. The need of harmonics minimization is required in the current inverter. The SHEPWM is one of technique that widely used which has an advantage on selectable the harmonic order to be eliminated and operates on lower switching frequency scheme, leading benefit to decrease switching loss. The low pass filter is still highly required to minimize harmonics from SHEPWM inverter output. The LC low pass filter is selected which is highly efficient on harmonic elimination and improve the quality of the output. The SHEPWM and LC filter are performed simulation in PSIM. To avoid the difficulty of solving the SHEPWM non-linear equation and reduce the step to find the filter components, the ANN is proposed to simplify the process of design and simulation which provide the LC filter value from the desired parameters by using MATALB Simulink. The 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> with 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>, 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> with 7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> and 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> with 9<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonics order are proposed in simulation scope with fixed value of capacitor 100 uF, 220 uF and 330uF and total harmonic distortion (THD) from 2% to 5% to be totally 270 ANN training data. The simulation result of 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> and 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> elimination of harmonic order is lower THD than other for the output before filter and the 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> and 9<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> elimination of harmonic order are required less LC filter value than other to achieve same THD. The parameter value from ANN model comparing with simulation in PSIM are analyzed and result in the lowest error at 0.27% and the highest at 1.51% from assigned testing value. The concept of using ANN is presented which be possible solution to apply. However, the result has such a bit of error that indicating a greater number of training data is required to achieve more accuracy in ANN model.

articleTitle: Deep ANN-based RF-MRAS for Speed-Sensorless Indirect Field Oriented Control of Induction Motor Drive for Electric Vehicles
abstract: This paper applies a deep neural network to rotor flux-based field-oriented control of an induction motor drive for electric vehicles. The proposed technique uses a deep neural network in a model reference adaptive system (MRAS) to estimate rotor speed. The proposed MRAS consists of a reference and adaptive model with a learning mechanism. The proposed MRAS with a deep neural network allows an accurate approximation of non-linearity and increases the system's response time. The performance of the proposed approach is validated on different scenarios, namely, vehicle acceleration conditions, constant speed, uneven road surface conditions, and deceleration modes. The dynamic performance is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink. The experimental results demonstrate the proposed method's advantages over conventional PI-based approaches for controlling sensorless induction drives for electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Constant DC Current Source Using Asymmetrical SRC Operated in Discontinuous Conduction Mode
abstract: This paper presents a converter that provides constant output current. This converter is implemented by using asymmetrical series resonant converter (SRC) operated in discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) with variable switching frequency control. It is shown in the paper the output current only depends on input voltage and switching frequency. Hence, the load condition does not have any effect on the load current during steady state. However, there is one condition that the output voltage has to be lower than the input voltage. In addition, the proposed converter also provides common ground between input and output. With diode configuration setting at the output, the proposed converter has a capability to be selected for noninverting (positive) and inverting (negative) output. Common ground is still remained for both configurations. State-plane diagram representing steady state response of the converter is presented. It is also shown that the proposed converter during steady state is also analyzed by utilizing state-plane diagram technique. Example for converter design is also presented together with computer simulation that confirms the analytical work.

articleTitle: Steering Angle Prediction for Self-Driving Car Using Proposed CNN Architecture
abstract: Automobiles offer significant advantages in terms of convenience, time efficiency, privacy, and cargo capacity. However, they also present challenges such as high maintenance costs, parking difficulties, and, most notably, reliance on human drivers, whose decision-making can be compromised by various factors. This often leads to road accidents, with human error contributing to over half of these incidents. To resolve this issue, this study proposes creating a deep learning-based model that adjusts the steering angle when a vehicle deviates from its lane. With the advantages of convolutional neural networks (CNNs), the proposed model aims to predict and correct steering angles in real-time, thereby enhancing vehicle control and reducing the risk of accidents. As shown by the experimental results, the proposed model secured an accuracy of 82% in predicting steering angles during testing, demonstrating its effectiveness in learning, and generalizing steering angle adjustments. The operational performance of the model will be assessed through comparison with the predicted and actual steering angles, which will be visualized through simulated driving video data. Therefore, the primary objective is to minimize human error in driving, thereby ensuring safer and more reliable transportation solutions.

articleTitle: Broadband Slit-Cut Square-Shaped Meta-Surface Slot-Coupled Antenna for C-Band Radar Technology
abstract: This research proposes a very low-complexity broadband meta-surface slot antenna for C-band radar technology. A 4 × 6 uniformly square-shaped meta-surface scheme was on the upper-layered substrate. The meta-surface scheme has been slit-cut in vertical and horizontal lines for impedance bandwidth (IBW) improvement. Besides, slit-cut lines contributed to match impedance around 6.4 GHz and 7 GHz, giving rise to wide IBW. On lower-layered substrates, the slot-coupled sat at the center of the ground plane with a Y-shaped microstrip-line feed on the other side. The simulated results of IBW and gain variation were between 4.63 – 8.33 GHz and 5.78 – 9.33 dBic. The maximum gain was 9.33 dBic at 6 GHz. The proposed slit-cut meta-surface antenna achieved a wideband IBW, rendering it operational for C-band radar applications.

articleTitle: CMA of Non-uniform Metasurface Circularly-Polarized Slotted-Patch Antenna with L-Shaped Feed Structure
abstract: This research presents a non-uniform metasurface (MTS) scheme circularly-polarized slotted-patch (CPSP) antenna for modern cellular technology. The proposed non-uniform MTS CPSP antenna was combined with non-uniform MTS scheme (upper-layer substrate) and slot-coupled feed (lower-layer substrate). The slot-coupled feed comprised of the L-shaped microstrip-line feed and rhombus-slotted ground plane. The non-uniform MTS scheme was characterized using characteristic mode analysis (CMA). The CP mode at 4.6 GHz (center frequency) was realized by two orthogonal modes (modes 1 and 2). To achieve wide return loss bandwidth (RLBW), the use of the different sizes (two sizes) of square-shaped MTS unit cells was adopted. The simulated RLBW and axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) results achieved 34.78% (between 4.1 – 5.7 GHz) and 5.65% (between 4.43 – 4.69 GHz). The optimal gain of right-hand circular polarization was 3.56 dBic at 4.35 GHz, rendering this proposed non-uniform MTS CPSP antenna is functional for wireless communications.

articleTitle: 2D LiDAR-Based Eucalyptus Tree Measurement and Monitoring System using Mobile Application
abstract: LiDAR technology has rapidly advanced, offering highly accurate solutions for tree geometry estimation, which is particularly valuable in agriculture and forestry. Its ability to capture precise 2D and 3D data has revolutionized tree detection and measurement. In Eucalyptus plantations, continuous monitoring is critical to maximizing growth, enhancing paper production, and mitigating environmental damage. However, existing solutions face challenges in real-time monitoring due to factors such as parasitic interference, low-light conditions, and uneven terrain. In this work, we present a novel, end-to-end framework that enhances Eucalyptus tree measurement and monitoring. Our framework significantly improves data collection efficiency by allowing measurements at walking speed, reducing measurement distance by 50% compared to traditional manual approaches. This system integrates 2D-LiDAR with additional environmental sensors to extract key tree parameters, including circumference, position, and tree count. The collected data is stored in real-time and uploaded to a centralized server for further analysis. Experimental evaluations across 160 trees, under five distinct farm conditions, demonstrate that our system achieves 89% accuracy in tree diameter estimation and 98.5% accuracy in tree counting, significantly outperforming traditional methods. These results establish our framework as a highly effective solution for improving the accuracy and efficiency of tree monitoring in challenging environments.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Field study of Solar EV Charging Power Transmission Line Using the 3D Finite Element Method
abstract: This paper present a study on the electromagnetic field of a power transmission line used for solar EV charging through the 3D Finite Element Method (FEM) by varying the conductor material type. The study is divided into four parts: beginning with the design of the study area's elements, followed by the exploration of approximation functions within 3D elements, the creation of element equations, and finally, the simulation of electromagnetic field distribution. The approach involves dividing the study area using tetrahedral elements (it is a shape with the least number of nodes and connections), applying equations derived from element-based approximations, and solving them in MATLAB. The study's results indicate that the conductor type affects the electromagnetic field values (favored by transmission line), with the minimum fields at a 1-meter distance from the source being 1.2357 µT for copper (Cu) and 1.2339 µT for aluminum (Al). Both conductor types exhibit electromagnetic field values at a 1meter distance from the source (throughout the day) that do not exceed the ICNIRP standard.

articleTitle: Application of BCITL-Based Wireless-Power-Transmission (WPT) Model for Moisture Sensors
abstract: In this paper, an application of wireless-power-transmission (WPT) technology in moisture sensors of materials under test (MUTs) is introduced. A WPT model based on a bi-characteristic-impedance transmission line (BCITL) is employed to analyze the WPT in the presence of MUTs. Using the simulated and measured data, the WPT model of the ultra high frequency radio frequency identification (UHF-RFID) system operating in the 920–925 MHz frequency band was developed. The MUT dielectric constant was varied from 10 to 30, according to the MUT's moisture content of interest. The new BCITL-based WPT model can produce accurate results with an additional physical understanding based on simulated results. In addition, the WPT technique can be used to indicate the moisture level of MUTs.

articleTitle: Energy Conservation of Electrical Machines in Local Plant Factory Using Preventive Maintenancene and State Estimation
abstract: This paper investigates the application of predictive maintenance strategies, state estimation techniques, and the cumulative maintenance cost function to enhance energy conservation in electrical machines within a local plant factory in Nakhon Phanom province, Thailand. The research methodology encompasses a comprehensive site survey, problem analysis, and the development and implementation of targeted solutions. Focusing on motor fault detection, the study employs current and vibration signal analysis to monitor machine health. Results indicate that excessive vibration levels frequently lead to ball bearing damage and subsequent electrical malfunctions. By implementing vibration monitoring and utilizing the cumulative maintenance cost function, motor degradation can be effectively anticipated, allowing for preventive measures that improve reliability and optimize maintenance costs over time. This predictive maintenance approach has practical applications in industrial environments, offering potential improvements in energy efficiency, extending equipment lifespan, and managing long-term maintenance expenses.

articleTitle: A New IoT-Based Smart Greenhouse for Cultivation of Water Convolvulus
abstract: This paper presents a new IOT system for monitoring and controlling plant cultivation in greenhouse system. The system aims to regulate and monitor the environmental conditions suitable for plant cultivation in real-time. The system utilizes sensors to measure environmental conditions, such as soil moisture sensor, light intensity sensor, temperature sensor, and air humidity sensor. The Node MCU ESP32 is used for processing and controlling these operations. The system is designed to send notifications through Line application and allows farmers to monitor the system's performance and plant growth in real-time via a smartphone application. It can utilize the Blynk IoT application on a smartphone for remotely monitoring and controlling the environmental conditions and provides historical data. This experiment demonstrates that the designed system can successfully cultivate plants and promote better growth compared to traditional cultivation methods with a 13.38% improvement. Additionally, it provides convenience and ease of management for plant cultivation.

articleTitle: Ripeness Classification of Fresh Oil Palm Using Deep Learning
abstract: The challenge of accurately ripeness level classifying from fresh oil palm fruit, this research investigated the problems and methods that were used in ripeness level classification. The goal of this research is to present a method for classifying the ripeness levels of oil palm fruits using deep learning techniques applied to image data. This research applies a deep learning model for classifying the ripeness level of fresh oil palm fruit and aiming for real-time application or mobile usage. The proposed model, Yolov9n (nano), adapts principles from convolutional neural networks that was tuned the learning parameters consist of the Adam optimizer, a learning rate of 0.001, and a batch size of 32, result in the most accurate ripeness level classification model. The research demonstrates the Yolov9n (nano) improved model with optimized parameters to achieve the highest accuracy. Training and validation datasets represent precision of 99.4%, recall of 99.6%, mean average precision at 50% (mAP50) of 99.5%, and mAP50-95 of 92.6%. These findings confirm the model’s effectiveness in accurately classifying the ripeness level of oil palm fruit from images. The study provides guidance for the practical deep learning implementation of ripeness level classification on fresh oil palm imaging for efficient harvesting by farmers cultivating oil palm.

articleTitle: Development of a Phase-Locked Loop Circuit in Running Frequency Mode for Capacitance-to-Voltage Conversion
abstract: Capacitance-to-voltage conversion is essential for capacitive sensors in various industries, including touch interfaces, medical devices, and moisture measurement. However, circuit design faces challenges like non-linearity, noise, and small capacitance variations affecting voltage signals. This article proposes a phase-locked loop in free-running oscillator mode with a frequency-to-voltage converter to enhance accuracy and stability. Test results show a 97.9% measurement accuracy, demonstrating reduced noise and improved stability. The proposed circuit is ideal for high-precision applications in diverse environments, overcoming limitations of traditional methods.

articleTitle: Hybrid fuel cell and supercapacitor system with backstepping control for energy management
abstract: The paper presents a method to control autonomous energy sources, hybridizing fuel cells and supercapacitors supplying a resistive load. As it is an autonomous system, there are no longer other interactions with outside systems; it takes full advantage of using a backstepping control where its global stability is guaranteed. Simulation results are given to demonstrate well-known hybrid operating modes and the constraints of fuel cells as a primary energy source.

articleTitle: A Bidirectional LCC-S Compensator on Wireless Power Transfer with Constant Voltage
abstract: This paper studies a bidirectional wireless power transfer (BD-WPT) system designed for electric vehicles (EVs) operating at 400V input, 350V output, 11kW, and 85kHz. The bidirectional power electronic devices that function as inverters or rectifiers with relays are employed to alter the direction of power flow between the source and the vehicle in the bidirectional DC-DC converter, which utilizes the LCC-S resonant circuit that is designed separately for the source and vehicle. MATLAB/Simulink is used to conduct the validation. The output voltage on both the source and the vehicle sides can be regulated to a specific level.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Resonant Converters for EV Charging Applications
abstract: The wide applications of Electric Vehicles (EVs) for integration with renewable energy sources need high-power, isolated bidirectional converters (IBC). Bi-directional converters often suffer from high switching power losses leading to efficiency reduction. Therefore many topologies are proposed to achieve soft switching and increase the converter efficiency. Among the available topologies, resonant converters (RC), such as LLC, CLLC, CLLLC, and dual active bridge (DAB) converters, are widely employed for high-power conversion because of their superior efficiency and soft-switching capabilities. In this article, a comprehensive comparative performance analysis of different RC topologies is presented. Among these, the CLLLC converter topology has emerged as a promising solution, offering higher efficiency and an extended soft-switching range compared to other RCs. Performance validation of various RCs is obtained through an experimental prototype.

articleTitle: Enhanced Distribution Network Restoration Using Tabu Search with Load Prioritization
abstract: This paper presents a Tabu Search-based optimization framework designed for restoring service in electrical distribution networks following a fault. The primary goal is to maximize load restoration while minimizing the number of switch operations necessary to isolate and recover from a faulted section. A priority-based restoration scheme is incorporated to prioritize critical loads, such as hospitals and emergency services, using a weighted restoration approach. Upon the occurrence of a fault, the affected branch is isolated, and the Tabu Search algorithm identifies feasible switching configurations that restore power without reconnecting the faulted branch.The proposed method is tested on both a modified IEEE 33-bus distribution network and a real-world network operated by the Provincial Electricity Authority (PEA) in Ubonratchathani, Thailand. In the IEEE network, distributed generation (DG) units are included to enhance system resilience, while the PEA network enables validation in a realistic operational environment with varied load types. A penalty factor is applied to discourage excessive switching, promoting a solution that balances effective load restoration with operational simplicity. The framework’s performance is assessed by evaluating the total restored load and the number of required switch operations, demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing reliability and continuity in both theoretical and real-world distribution networks.

articleTitle: Classifying Immature fruit Using Brewster’s Angle
abstract: This paper presents a nondestructive technique to classify immature fruits. An identification methodology is based on Brewster’s angle to determine the stage of maturity of a fruit, which can be obtained from angle of incidence where the least reflection occurs. In addition, Brewster’s angle technique is applied with dual frequency system. The simulation results show that Brewster’s angle changes with the stage of maturity of the fruit.

articleTitle: Recommended Measurement Positions for Urine Volume Estimation via Conductivity Analysis
abstract: Urinary bladder dysfunction, characterized by the inability to control bladder muscles or perceive bladder fullness accurately, significantly impacts the quality of life and poses risks such as infections or urethral injury due to overfilling. Clean intermittent catheterization (CIC) is commonly used to manage bladder emptying but carries risks like urinary tract infections and urethral damage. Non-invasive monitoring of bladder volume can reduce the need for CIC and associated risks. Conductivity measurement is an alternative technique for estimating bladder volume by analyzing impedance changes. However, the electrode positions for measuring the conductivity in the previous studies are performed at the abdomen where this position could be affected by the intestine or the uterus. In this study, eight electrode positions were investigated including the front, back, and sides. A method to compute the total response utilizing the measurement voltage from the front and the back positions is also proposed. Six bladder sizes, ranging from 164 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> to 417 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, were simulated, and voltage responses to the volume change were determined. Results indicate that electrode placement and the enlargement of the bladder significantly affect the amplitude and the correlation between the voltage and the bladder volume. The front positions provided the highest amplitude but were unable to sense in some cases. The back, left, and right positions provided good response but were inferior in response linearity. However, the proposed total voltage could effectively reflect the volume while the linearity was significantly improved.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Electrostatic Precipitator Featuring a Rotating Particle Collection Plate for Home Air Purification
abstract: In contrast to many popular HEPA and fiber- filter based air purifiers in the existing market for dealing with fine particulate matter of 2.5 microns or less (PM2.5) in the household, this paper illustrates a modified electrostatic precipitator (ESP) based air purification design for home-use. A rotating module is embedded to the particle collecting plate along with a proper brushing mechanism to remove the dust and other fine particles from the plate to the dust bin at the bottom. This modification potentially improves the efficiency of the ESP air purifier in the household by continuously removing the dust off the collecting plate. The design selects low-cost materials and simple electronics parts to save the cost of the prototyping and the eventual manufacturing cost. The electrodes consist of a horizontal panel of copper wires and a rotating cylindrical aluminum plates underneath at the operating voltage of 1,300 volts. A 12-Vdc cooling fan is used for increasing inlet-outlet air flow. Also, a 12-Vdc geared motor turning slowly at 5 rpm is driving the rotation module inside the cylindrical aluminum plate. A 220-Vac to 12-Vdc 2A switching power supply is the energy source for this prototype. The efficiency of device is examined and evaluated in the closed and confined volume against the generated incense smoke. The results have shown that the rotating module immediately improves the function of the collecting plate and hence, increases the filtration efficiency. It has also been found that air flow speed has positive effect on the modified ESP efficiency.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Cultivation of Mitragyna Speciosa
abstract: This paper proposes a smart farm system, applying to cultivate mitragyna speciosa plants in Thailand. The greenhouse system with several sensors, microcontroller, and cultivation devices has been designed. The temperature, light intensity and moisture in the area of cultivation can be measured and the microcontroller has been used to read all data and then they are shown through the website. The cultivation data have been processed and then used for controlling temperature, light intensity and moisture inside the greenhouse. The proposed system is very effective, that the temperature values, light intensity, and humidity can be monthly, daily and hourly viewed and displayed on the computer and smartphone. When the proposed system has been applied for cultivating mitragyna speciose, the better growth results have been found comparing with the traditional cultivation.

articleTitle: A Development of Fabric Electrodes for Long-term Respiration Monitoring
abstract: The Ag/AgCl electrode is one of the most commonly used electrodes for determining respiration activity. Although it is easy to use, Ag/AgCl electrodes are disposable and may not be suitable for long-term use or conditions involving body movement. This study explores the effectiveness of wearable fabric electrodes for respiratory monitoring. Fabric electrodes were developed, and the bioimpedance of the thorax was measured for monitoring respiration function. The correlation between the bioimpedance obtained using the developed fabric electrodes and commercial Ag/AgCl electrodes was investigated. Three experimental conditions with varying body movements were implemented: resting, exercising by riding a training bicycle, and post-exercising. The results revealed a strong correlation (with an average correlation of 0.88) between the fabric and Ag/AgCl electrodes across all conditions, confirming their potential as viable alternatives. The resting condition provided the highest correlation (r = 0.93), while the exercising condition exhibited the lowest correlation (r = 0.84). The fabric electrodes demonstrated significant advantages in reusability, reduced skin irritation, and long-term firm attachment. However, when using a strap to hold the fabric electrodes in place, attachment challenges in high-curvature thorax areas led to reduced signal quality during exercise.

articleTitle: A First-order All-pass Filter Based on LT1228 and Its Application
abstract: This paper proposes a first-order all-pass filter (APF) that employs two LT1228s, a resistor, and a grounded capacitor to be implemented via commercially available integrated circuits. The phase response of the proposed filter is electronically controllable by modifying the transconductance value via the biasing current of the OTA (IB1). The oscillator quadrature sinusoidal signal circuit is generated by the proposed APF, which includes an integrator. The efficacy of the sinusoidal oscillator circuit and the proposed APF is validated through the use of experimental results and simulations. The results that were obtained are in strong agreement with the theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: Application of Deep Neural Network for NOMA Systems in 5G Communications
abstract: Currently, multi-channel access techniques may not be able to effectively handle massive data situations. For 5G communication systems, non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) can improve channel efficiency to support more users. However, in the transmitter, the complete channel state information (CSI) is required, while in the receiver, the computational complexity is high, which is the main disadvantage of NOMA system. The use of deep neural network (DNN) as a deep learning (DL) technique is an excellent solution to deal with various problems. In this work, DNN predicts parameter values to perform channel estimation in NOMA systems. From the results, the performance in terms of symbol error rate (SER) can be improved higher than standard estimation approach.

articleTitle: Observer-less Fixed-Time Speed Control For Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors with matched-mismatched disturbances
abstract: This paper presents a state-dependent Variable Exponent Coefficient Sliding Mode Control (VECFSMC) By inducing fixed-time stability analysis, the proposed state-dependent sliding surface provides not only system stability but also a quick response in a fixed period of time as well as counteract with matched and mismatched disturbances. The proposed sliding mode control strategy does not use observers to estimate the disturbances. The designed sliding mode surface possesses robustness properties which is sufficient to cope with both matched and mismatch disturbances in a period of fixed time. Firstly, the mathematical model of permanent magnet synchronous motor and the mathematical background of variable exponent coefficient are demonstrated theoretically. Secondly, the state-dependent sliding surface with variable exponent coefficient is designed. The controller that can manipulate both the speed of PMSM and matched-mismatched disturbances is constructed. Lyapunov function is applied to assess the stability of the proposed method. Finally, a numerical simulation with PMSM drive shows fast convergence, good robustness against both matched and mismatched disturbances. The proposed fixed-time controller with this observer-less method offers high efficiency and offers not too complicated control solution comparing to the other fixed-time and finite-time methods with a small number of parameters.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Algorithms for Predicting the Remaining Useful Life of Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are widely used in portable devices, electric vehicles, and large-scale energy storage systems. Predicting remaining useful life (RUL) of these batteries is crucial for ensuring the reliability and safe operation of battery-powered systems. This study aims to identify the most effective method for prediction RUL by evaluating predictions derived form the CALCE dataset. We compare the performance of Bi-LSTM, a deep learning algorithm, with model-based approaches (Kalman filter) and data-driven methods (Support Vector Machine: SVM), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). Data processing will vary based on the type of non-linearity being analyzed. Model performance will be assessed using validation metrics such as RMSE, MAE, and relative error. The evaluation indicates that while other models enhance the temporal dependence of battery data, Bi-LSTM consistently outperforms them in accuracy and in capturing the temporal and nonlinear relationships within the data. This research is significant for identifying effective machine learning strategies to enhance the performance and reliability of lithium-ion battery management systems (IBMS).

articleTitle: Auto-tuned Active Filter Design for Lighting System in Buildings
abstract: The lighting system is a continuously used energy system found in all buildings. This system is highly complex as it includes various types such as incandescent bulbs, fluorescent tubes, HID lamps, and LEDs. These types of loads consist of many electronic components and are significant sources of Auto-Tuned Active Filter signals. These harmonic signals directly affect protective devices and electronic equipment in the building's electrical system. Therefore, reducing the harmonic signals generated by the lighting system is crucial for buildings. Generally, harmonic reduction can be achieved by installing one of three types of filters: active, passive, and hybrid. This research presents the design of an auto-tuned active filter using the MATLAB Simulink and tests it using four lighting load cases. The designed circuit can effectively reduce harmonic signals while also improving the energy efficiency of the building.

articleTitle: Thai voice language encryption and decryption using 3DES and AES algorithm for communication
abstract: The aim of this paper is to compare the performance of the encryption and decryption of Thai voice language by using Triple Data Encryption Standard (3DES) and Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) algorithms for secure communication. The research methodology involves collecting Thai voice samples, converting speech to text by using Google’s API to be applied with cryptography algorithms. Performance comparison between 3DES and AES focuses on accuracy and processing time. Experimental results demonstrate 100% accuracy in preserving original text content for both algorithms. However, AES consistently outperforms 3DES in processing speed, particularly for larger data sizes. The study reveals a linear relationship between input size and processing time for both algorithms. Furthermore, the findings imply that AES offers superior performance in terms of speed and security for encrypting Thai voice data, making it more suitable for secure communication applications. Therefore, this research contributes to improve data security in Thai voice communications by providing empirical evidence on the efficacy of modern encryption standards.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Coal and Biomass Mixtures in a Traveling Grate Commercial Steam Boiler
abstract: An industrial steam boiler is a steam-generating device made of steel, designed as a closed chamber with a capacity of over 1,000 liters and a pressure exceeding six times atmospheric pressure. The steam produced is used in various industries, including electricity generation, drying processes, sterilization, and pasteurization. Boilers are classified into three types: fire-tube boilers, water-tube boilers, and hybrid boilers. They can operate using various fuels, such as liquid fuels (e.g., diesel oil, heavy oil), gaseous fuels (e.g., LPG, NGV), and solid fuels (e.g., coal, biomass). An analysis of fuel combustion in boilers reveals notable variations in emissions, pollution levels, heat cost per unit, and steam quality. This study focused on a traveling grate water-tube boiler powered by bituminous coal, which is popular due to its advantages: compact size, ease of installation and maintenance, moderate heat output, and lower heat cost compared to other types. However, it has some drawbacks, including difficulties in maintaining consistent heat levels, which can lead to uneven temperatures and unstable steam pressure. Additionally, adjusting the fuel feed rate is slow, causing delayed responses, and the combustion process generates smoke and sulfur dioxide gas. The aim of this research was to improve traditional solid-fuel boilers by enabling them to use mixed fuels, specifically converting them to boilers that utilize a coal-biomass powder blend. The biomass component, which uses readily available agricultural residues, was incorporated to address the limitations of solid fuels. The results showed that pure coal fuel provided an efficiency of 63.01%, while the coal-biomass blend achieved an efficiency of 78.2%. Toxic gas emissions were reduced by 8%, and the use of the coal-biomass mix saved 52.675 kilograms of fuel per hour, resulting in an annual fuel cost reduction of 16,565,871 THB.

articleTitle: Improving Load Frequency Control in Power Systems by Optimizing PID Controllers with the Brown Bear Algorithm
abstract: The goal of this study is to improve the PID controller parameters for a two-area cogeneration power plant system by using three optimization techniques: the Genetic Algorithm (GA), the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Brown Bear Optimization Algorithm (BOA). The tuning of the PID controller was evaluated using MATLAB R2024B on a system equipped with an AMD Ryzen 7 7735HS processor, an RTX 4050 graphics card and 32 GB of RAM. The results show that the BOA is better than both the GA and the PSO at finding the best PID parameters, especially for the IAE (Integral of Absolute Error) and ITAE (Integral of Time-weighted Absolute Error) objective functions. The BOA demonstrated improved effectiveness in stabilizing frequency deviations while also minimizing both settling time and error within the system. The enhanced performance of the PID controller through BOA leads to greater stability and efficiency in power generation and distribution, thereby fostering a more dependable automatic power generation control system. This investigation emphasizes the promise of the BOA as a valuable instrument for enhancing PID controllers in extensive interconnected power systems.

articleTitle: Weapon Detection Method Using Convolutional Neural Network with Human Pose Estimation
abstract: The increasing incidence of violent events involving weapons highlights the urgent need for advanced technologies to prevent and forewarn individuals. Currently, closed-circuit television (CCTV) systems are widely utilized to document incidents for use as evidence; however, these systems lack the capability to prevent, detect, or notify stakeholders of incidents in real time. This study proposes the development of a new system designed to monitor and mitigate violent incidents involving weapons by proposing an innovative method to improve the accuracy of weapon detection within CCTV frameworks. The proposed method initially detects weapons within sequential images. In instances where detection fails, the system employs a human pose estimation model to reassess the potential presence of weapons. Upon identifying a detected individual, the system utilizes an adaptive pose region to refine the area of interest for further weapon detection. From experimental results, the proposed method significantly improves performance metrics, achieving average values of 92% in precision, 91% in recall, and 92% in F1-score on the testing dataset. These findings underscore the effectiveness of the proposed system in detecting and identifying weapons associated with violent incidents, thereby contributing to the prevention of future violent events.

articleTitle: Wideband Four-Element L-Shaped Notch-Patch MIMO Antenna for 5G NR Networks
abstract: This work proposes simply wideband four-element L-shaped notch-patch (LNP) MIMO antenna for 5G new radio (NR) networks. The proposed LNP MIMO antenna comprised of four-port antenna elements. The single antenna scheme contained L-shaped with notch microstrip patch antenna and modified ground plane. The proposed LNP MIMO antenna at 4.5 GHz (center frequency) can be provided impedance bandwidth (IBW) of 64% (3.57 – 6.45 GHz). The LNP MIMO antenna has been evaluated the MIMO performance metrics, including transmission coefficient (isolation), envelop correlation coefficient (ECC), diversity gain (DG), and mean effective gain (MEG). The simulated results of the LNP MIMO antenna achieved isolation of 20 dB, ECC of below 0.005, DG of above 9.975 dB, and MEG of approximately -3 dB. All simulated results are in good satisfactory, rendering the proposed LNP MIMO antenna suitable for 5G applications.

articleTitle: Development of an Electric Taekwondo Armor for Training with a Wireless System and Real-Time Scoring Display
abstract: This paper proposes the development of an electric Taekwondo armor system designed for training with a wireless communication framework and real-time scoring display. The system utilizes ESP8266 microcontrollers and piezoelectric sensors to detect impacts and transmit data using the ESP-NOW protocol, achieving a communication range exceeding 100 meters. The system consists of a transmitter embedded within red and blue armor and a receiver that displays scores on an LED P10 display. Experimental results demonstrate the system's efficiency, with an average success rate of 76.67 percent for red armor and 84.45 percent for blue armor during controlled kicking tests. The system also performs reliably within the dimensions of a standard Taekwondo competition field, validating its practical application for both individual training and combat practice. This innovation provides a cost-effective and accurate solution to enhance athletes' performance by improving scoring precision and enabling focused skill development.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Multi-Bit Input Logic Blocks in RTL-Designed FPGA Architecture: A Framework for FPGA and ASIC Integration
abstract: This paper explores the evaluation and optimization of multi-bit input logic blocks (LBs) within RTL-designed FPGA architectures. Traditional FPGA designs face limitations in power consumption, delay, and area due to the constraints of reconfigurable circuits. The proposed architecture leverages RTL-level design capabilities to address these challenges and enables the co-design of FPGAs and ASICs. The authors evaluate the performance of 8-bit, 16-bit, and 32-bit input LBs in terms of delay, area, and synthesis feasibility. The results demonstrate that 8-bit input LBs achieve a delay of 0.68 ns with an area of 2202.48 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, outperforming multi-stage smaller LBs. Although 16-bit input LBs show potential for delay reduction, their synthesis demands significant time and results in a large area footprint, rendering them impractical. Synthesis of 32-bit input LBs was not feasible due to current tool limitations. These findings highlight the effectiveness of 8-bit input LBs for pattern matching tasks and emphasize the importance of application-specific optimization. The fixed routing feature of RTL-designed FPGAs facilitates the development of efficient, customizable designs tailored to specific workloads. This work contributes to the advancement of FPGA architectures, offering insights for future research on larger input LBs and their integration into high-performance applications.

articleTitle: Multitask Diffusion Adaptive Tuning Affine Projection Algorithm for Distributed Model
abstract: This paper presents combine-then-adapt diffusion model on affine projection adaptive algorithm with adaptive tuning mechanism. An adaptive affine projection algorithm is suggested in the distributed network. Diffusion strategy involves with the combination stage and adaptation stage. By adding the extra-stage in the combination stage, the combination between nodes and inside nodes are built with the global cost function for multitask model to eliminate unknown data. As dealt with fast convergence, the adaptive tuning parameters are assigned in terms of step-size value. Experimental results reveal that this proposed algorithm is able to contribute the approving results for system identifications.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Current Controlled Battery Charger Using DCM Asymmetrical SRC and Boost-Buck Converters
abstract: This paper presents a converter system with bidirectional operation. The objective of this converter system is to transfer energy between a battery and a DC bus, each of which has a nearly constant voltage. This research work uses a series resonant converter (SRC) operated in discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) connected in cascade configuration with a two-switch boost-buck converter. With SRC operated in DCM providing constant current and boost-buck converter providing a wide range of gain, the proposed system has the flexibility to match several values of battery and DC bus with constant current supply and common ground between both ends. The proposed system can do forward operation, from batter to DC bus, as well as, backward operation, from DC bus to battery (battery charging). In this paper, the analysis and design examples of the proposed system are given. The computer simulation to confirm the analytical work is also included.

articleTitle: Real Time Energy Monitoring and Location Tracking System for Medical Equipment Management in Hospital
abstract: The efficient utilization of high value and mobile/portable medical equipment is a key towards improving hospital’s operations and costs. In this study, a real time energy monitoring and location tracking system for medical equipment is developed and deployed in Thammasat University hospital in Pathumthani province. An embedded device in form of a smart plug is prototyped with a current sensor, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) wireless interface, WiFi wireless interface, and a microcontroller to monitor the energy usage of a medical equipment and to track its location, simultaneously. The smart plug is acting as an electronics tag which can be tracked within the service area of our previously developed real time location tracking system which consists of a group of location tracking devices called anchors and a location server on a public cloud computing system. The energy usage data for each medical equipment is estimated and reported to the server. The staffs of the medical equipment department of the hospital can locate any equipment and monitor its energy usage status remotely over the internet. Energy utilization and movement records can be used for later data analysis.

articleTitle: Pneumonia and Covid-19 Detection on Chest X-ray Imaging Using Deep Learning: PCX-Net
abstract: Pneumonia and COVID-19 are severe diseases that primarily affect the lungs, causing acute and significant respiratory distress. In clinical settings, patients are screened to differentiate between these two conditions using computerized chest X-ray imaging. To address this issue, researchers have explored the solutions based on deep learning model to automatic analysis on the chest X-ray images. This research evaluates the four neural network models consist of VGG16, ResNet50, MobileNet, and Xception to classify the chest X-ray images on three categories: pneumonia, COVID-19, and normal lungs. This research involved preprocessing three datasets of chest X-ray images, including artifact removal, image resizing, and data augmentation, prior to model training and testing processing. From our experimental results, Xception model demonstrated the highest performance, achieving training accuracy of 99.99%, validation accuracy of 98.00%, training loss of 0.15%, and validation loss of 7.42%, with an overall accuracy of 97.70%. Thus, the Xception model is the most effective for distinguishing and predicting lung conditions from chest X-ray images and should be considered for future applications in medical data analysis.

articleTitle: Temperature Analysis and Simulation in Microwave Systems with TE20 Waveguide Using 3D Finite Element Method
abstract: This research focuses on developing a mathematical model to analyze the temperature distribution within a microwave oven system using a TE₂₀ waveguide and the 3D Finite Element Method. The study examines the operation of a stationary tray microwave oven with one-way and three-way waveguide configurations to compare the temperature distribution in food and assess the impact of the waveguide pattern on the steady-state temperature. Simulations were conducted at a frequency of 20,000 MHz and a power of 800 W using MATLAB software, with results presented in graphical form. The findings reveal that the three-way waveguide achieves a more uniform and faster temperature distribution compared to the one-way waveguide, demonstrating reduced temperature deviation, higher peak food temperatures, and shorter times to reach steady state. These results support the development of more efficient microwave oven designs, enhancing heat distribution and energy savings, with potential applications in the food industry and modern kitchen appliances.

articleTitle: Design of a Prototype Monitoring System for Poultry Security using IoT and Machine Learning
abstract: In recent years, animal welfare has become very popular to reduce the effects of livestock living in small spaces. Free-range chicken farms are one of the ways to treat chickens with care and less stress. Several recent technologies were employed to improve animal wellness and product quality. Internet of Things and Machine Learning were widely implemented in many applications. This paper presents the prototype design of the monitoring system for poultry security. Two types of chicken sounds, alarm and infection sounds, were used to create a classification model based on Google’s Teachable Machine. Three types of ESP32-based RFID reader nodes track chickens in the coop. All information and classification data were transmitted to the monitoring dashboard using the MQTT protocol. The experiment showed that the proposed concept is feasible for farms with 93.33% classification accuracy and 100% status monitoring.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Gaussian Process Regression Interpolation for Spherical Near-Field Measurements
abstract: This study presents a novel electromagnetic spherical near-field (NF) interpolation method based on Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) to address challenges associated with under-sampling in NF data acquisition. The proposed approach mitigates errors in far-field (FF) radiation pattern predictions caused by insufficient NF sampling. The NF-to-FF transformation employs spherical wave expansion with double numerical integration. A seven-patch array antenna was simulated in CST Microwave Studio, with NF sampling angles exceeding the limits of the spherical sampling theorem, resulting in a 25.65% under-sampling rate. Results demonstrate that GPR effectively reconstructs NF data, achieving FF radiation patterns closely matching those obtained directly from CST Microwave Studio. The absolute error is reduced to under 10% in the ZY plane and approximately 3% in the ZX plane. By enabling accurate FF radiation pattern predictions and reducing NF data acquisition time, the GPR-based method offers a robust and efficient solution for spherical NF measurements.

articleTitle: Fault Current Management Using Bidirectional DC/DC Converter in Smart DC Microgrid
abstract: The fault current contribution of distributed generators (DGs) is a main cause of misoperation of protection equipment. This paper proposes the fault current management using bidirectional DC/DC converter (BDC) for smart DC microgrid. The fault current contribution of DGs flows to the battery storage connected to the BDC. The total fault current amplitude is decreased to the grid current amplitude, and the fault current contribution does not disturb the coordination of protection equipment in the DC microgrid. According to the simulation results, the proposed fault current management can effectively decrease the total fault current amplitude to the grid current amplitude.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning and Machine Learning Approaches for Air Quality Prediction
abstract: Air quality prediction is crucial for addressing environmental challenges and mitigating health risks caused by pollution. This study provides a comparative analysis of Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) models for air quality classification. The dataset, comprising 5,000 samples from Dhaka, Bangladesh, was used to evaluate the performance of three ML models Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and three DL models VGG19, VGG16, and CNN1D. Key metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, were assessed to determine model performance. Results indicate that Random Forest achieved the highest accuracy among ML models (96%), demonstrating efficiency and stability in resource-constrained environments. Among DL models, VGG19 outperformed others with a comparable accuracy of 95%, showcasing its ability to handle complex patterns in air quality data. Learning curves further illustrated the rapid convergence of DL models, particularly VGG19, while ML models exhibited consistent performance across varying dataset sizes. This research highlights the trade-offs between computational efficiency and predictive performance in ML and DL approaches. It also underscores the importance of dataset diversity and scalability in building robust air quality prediction systems. Future work will explore hybrid techniques combining ML and DL to enhance adaptability and generalizability, as well as extend the dataset to include samples from multiple regions for more comprehensive analysis.

articleTitle: The Alternative FO-FIRLP-AF System for Eradication of Fix Value Impulsive Noise in Computer Representations
abstract: This philosophical article proposes the alternative First-Order Finite Impulse Response Linear Predictor with Average Filter (FO-FIRLP-AF) system, which is researched from the original First-Order Finite Impulse Response Linear Predictor with Median Filter (FO-FIRLP-SMF) system. Due to the verification outcomes, the productivity of the proposed alternative FO-FIRLP-AF system is better than previous prior state-of-art systems in objective assessment and subjective assessment at all noisy percentage, especially low and medium noisy percentage.

Author Keywords: A First-Order Linear Finite Impulse Response Linear Predictor (FO-FIRLP)

articleTitle: YOLOv7-Based Microplastic Detection: Crafting a Custom Dataset for Environmental Analysis
abstract: As the increase in plastic pollution rises, we face a significant setback of microplastics removal. The larger plastics are easily discarded but their smaller counterparts are indiscernible to the naked eye and in most cases take years to reduce. The presence of microplastics then creates innumerable health and environmental problems. To address this, we have used object detection models to detect and count microplastics using a novel dataset. The paper uses 3 versions of You Only Look Once model (YOLO) for the detection and counting of microplastics. Among them, YOLOv8 performed the best with 81.4%, followed by YOLOv7 with 80.73% and YOLOv9 with 77.2%. However, YOLOv7 performs best with test data and real-time detection.

articleTitle: Contingency Ranking and Analysis of Bhutan Network using Performance Index: Case Studies
abstract: Contingency ranking and analysis are essential tasks for system operators to ensure efficient power system operations and to maintain reliability. Through this process, operators can identify critical elements within the system whose failure could result in significant consequences, including potential blackouts in the worst-case scenario. In this paper, a single contingency ranking was conducted to determine the most critical components of Bhutan’s power system, followed by an analysis of the potential impacts of their outages. Based on the findings, appropriate solutions to mitigate the risk of blackouts are recommended.

articleTitle: Operational Three-Mode (3M) Algorithm for a Bi-Directional PEV Charger in G2V, V2H, and V2G Applications
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are widely recognized as one of the most effective strategies for reducing oil consumption and greenhouse gas emissions, establishing them as a key option for the future of road transportation. The widespread adoption of EVs is expected to have a profound societal impact, influencing various aspects of human life. A key advantage of EVs is their battery module, which offers a higher capacity compared to other devices. This high-capacity battery can also function as an energy storage system (ESS) for homes when connected to a charger. This paper presents the operational modes of a single-phase bi-directional plug-in electric vehicle (PEV) charger designed for G2V/V2H/V2G applications. The proposed system employs a bi-directional converter to facilitate two-way power flow between the home and the vehicle. The topology includes two stages: 1) a synchronous DC-DC converter and 2) a full-bridge AC-DC converter. The system operates in three modes: battery charging, energy backup, and grid-connected modes. Designed for a 7.7 kVA single-phase onboard charger, the system's feasibility is verified through simulations.

articleTitle: High Accuracy Fault Identification for High-Voltage Circuit Breakers using CGAN-1DCNN
abstract: High voltage vacuum circuit breakers are crucial for modern power systems in that they ensure the grid's stability. However, they could wear out and eventually fail due to their intricate design, operational, contact or actuator issues. This paper proposes a method to identify the faults for high voltage vacuum circuit breakers using Conditional Generative Adversarial Network-One-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (CGAN-1DCNN). The operational principle of the high-voltage vacuum circuit breaker was examined and a platform constructed to simulate fault scenarios. The data sets encompassed a range of fault types, including normal operation, trip upon closure, coil burnout, and others. CGAN was used to generate additional fault data, enhancing the model's generalization ability. 1DCNN was used to train deep learning on acquired data, diagnosing faults efficiently. The proposed method achieved relatively high precision of over 98% for fault identification compared to 86.30-96.34% of the traditional methods, which guarantee safe operation for the power systems.

articleTitle: The Practical Fallen of the Concrete Pole for Distribution System 24kV (MEA.) due to the impact of the Overhead Communication Cable
abstract: This article presents the analysis of the fallen of the MEA’s concrete pole through the influential communication cables by using the total bending moment method (BM.). Moreover, the BM. was analyzed at significant conditions such as the height of a concrete pole as 12 meters and the maximum BM. as 3500 kg*m and 5000 kg*m, the span distance as 20, 30, and 40 meters, respectively. Nowadays, The MEA’s concrete pole has been illustrated with the increasing communication cable which this problem may be causing the falling MEA’s concrete pole. Therefore, this article analyzes to determine the optimum number of communication cables for installation at the MEA’s concrete pole. Particularly, the communication cable in this case study is All Dielectric Self Support type (ADSS cable).

articleTitle: The Novel Outlier Extraordinariness Sensing and Recreation Operation Established on Adaptive MDBUTMF

Due to the simulation results, the performance of the proposed adaptive MDBUTMF operation is exceeding than all preceding operations at all outlier percentage in both PSNR and illustrational quality, especially at heavy outlier percentage.

articleTitle: Design of Miniaturized Metamaterial Reflector with Doubly Interdigital Structure for 5G Use Cases
abstract: This paper presents the design of a miniaturized metamaterial reflector composing of an open-loop transmission line unit cell structure. The transmission line ends are connected by using a double interdigital technique, resulting in a large capacitive value compared to the conventional methods. When combined with the open-loop line employing the trisection step-impedance structure with adjusting of the capacitive value, its second and third resonant frequencies will be controllable. As a result, this approach can reduce the unit cell size from a typical value of λ/2 to an approximate value of λ/16, therefore overall size of the reflector is significantly decreased. The designed unit cell is measured to be 1.05 cm × 1.0 cm. We implemented the proposed reflector on an FR-4 PCB with a relative permittivity of about 4.4, a substrate height (h) of 1.6 mm, and a loss tangent of about 0.02. The operating frequency range targets of 5G use cases were set to be at 1.8 GHz, 2.6 GHz and 3.5 GHz, respectively. When used with a dipole antenna, the bandwidths of 390 MHz, 604 MHz, and 1.1 GHz and the antenna gains of about 8.23 dB, 8.14 dB, and 8.19 dB were obtained at the operating frequencies, respectively.

articleTitle: Duty Cycle Balancing Technique for Three-Level Buck Converter Using Classic Buck Integration
abstract: This study focuses on balancing the duty cycle of a Three-Level Buck Converter by integration with the traditional Buck Converter. The suggested approach has the benefit of giving four outputs, each with its ground, except the module, which shares a ground with the input supply. Balancing the duty cycle ensures that all main switches function similarly, resulting in uniform heat dispersion across the switches. This lessens stress on the switches and considerably increases their longevity.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning Evaluation of Convolutional Neural Network Architectures for Thermal Image Classification of Solar Modules
abstract: Accurate anomaly classification in solar modules is crucial for efficient solar power system monitoring and maintenance. This study explores deep learning, specifically Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), for automated defect classification in thermal images. We employed transfer learning with pre-trained AlexNet and GoogleNet architectures, comparing static feature extraction and fine-tuning. Using a dataset of thermal images categorized as no anomaly, cracked, or soiled modules, the fully fine-tuned GoogleNet model achieved the highest classification accuracy 95.5%, outperforming AlexNet and traditional feature-based methods. GoogleNet's superior performance stems from its Inception modules, which learn more discriminative features by employing multiple convolutional filter sizes within the same layer, capturing complex thermal image patterns. Fine-tuning further boosts performance by adapting pre-trained knowledge to the specific task. These results demonstrate deep learning's potential for enhancing solar system maintenance reliability and efficiency.

articleTitle: The Novel Iterative Two-Stage Algorithm with Neighborhood Correlation for Removal the AAIN (Arbitrary Amplitude Impulse Noise)
abstract: Within outlier removal experimentation association, in the outlier revelation mechanism, the investigated figuring basis (which is located at the midpoint of the investigated window) and its neighborhood correlation (which is estimated from the investigated figuring basis and its encircling figuring basis) are theoretically elucidated as outlier correlation. In the simulated investigation, copious digital figures, which are compounded of F16 and Pepper under all random noise proportion, are engaged in the novel iterative two-stage algorithm in contemplating of the energetic of precedent state-of-art algorithms: MF, SMF, AMF and original 2-Stage system. From these simulated investigation products, the noise removal algorithm based on novel iterative 2-stage algorithm constitutes the exclusive energetic, which is contemplated with precedent state-of-art algorithms.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Analysis of Weighting Factors for Conditional and Importance Criteria in Gas Insulated Substation Health and Importance Indices
abstract: The effective maintenance of Gas Insulated Switchgear (GIS) in high-voltage (HV) substations is essential for ensuring system reliability and minimizing unplanned downtime. The percentage Health and Importance Indices (%HI and %ImI) are key metrics used to assess the criticality of various factors influencing GIS performance, such as equipment age, maintenance history, insulation quality, environmental conditions, and operational performance. This research performs a sensitivity analysis on the weighting factors applied to the %HI and %ImI, examining how changes in these weightings affect the indices. Using a weighting and scoring technique, the analysis investigates the impact of varying each parameter’s weight on the overall %HI and %ImI, identifying the most sensitive factors that influence maintenance decisions. The actual data for both the conditional factors and importance criteria are applied in these calculations. Subsequently, the actual scores of six units GIS are computed using ten different weighting sets. The results demonstrate that the weighting values follow a linear approach, where higher weight values indicate a greater influence on the respective criterion. In addition, the sensitivity of the weighting factors significantly impacts the process of adjusting the range for %HI and %ImI, ultimately affecting GIS health and importance identification and informing maintenance planning.

articleTitle: The Modelling and Control for Design Aero-Pendulum via Proportional–Integral–Derivative and Integral-Proportional Derivative
abstract: The article aims to clarify the essential design principles behind Aero pendulum balancing and its two related controllers: Proportional–Integral–Derivative (PID) and Integral-Proportional Derivative (I-PD). The design incorporates dynamic principles and Newton’s laws, leading to a non-linear mathematical model that must be converted into a linear form for effective control design. The PID controller serves as the primary controller, forming the foundation for developing I-PD controllers to ensure stability and the elimination of interference within the Aero pendulum system. MATLAB’s Simulink program is employed due to its smooth compatibility with the Arduino board and the Aero pendulum, facilitating simulation and experimentation. The controller’s logic capitalizes on the system’s capabilities to stabilize the Aero pendulum and sustain the targeted angle via simulation. The article explores the design of the controller based on the structural design derived from dynamic principles and parameters of Newton’s laws, assessing the angular performance of the Aero pendulum and its mathematical model-derived design while reviewing the control system’s performance index. Ultimately, the article focuses on using PID and I-PD controllers to stabilize the Aero pendulum, underlining how effective the non-linear equations from the mathematical model are in controlling and stabilizing the system. The findings reveal that the I-PD controller exhibits a higher amplitude with a time-setting point ranging from 2.1 to 2.3 seconds. In contrast, the PID controller demonstrates a lower amplitude than the PID controller, with a time-setting point of 2.3 to 2.5 seconds, making it slower than the I-PD controller.

articleTitle: A Simple Memristor with Passive Devices
abstract: The memristor is recognized as the fourth passive electrical component, complementing resistors, capacitors, and inductors. It establishes a direct relationship between electric charge and magnetic flux. As a bipolar passive element, the memristor exhibits nonlinear hysteresis behavior within a specific frequency range. Currently, there are no practical memristors available on the market, nor are there any models capable of operating across a sufficiently wide frequency band. This paper presents a model for the memristor using fundamental electrical elements and diodes. It is a simple model that demonstrates how the properties of a memristor can be derived from the properties of passive devices.

articleTitle: Realtime Implementation of Multiple Fault Detection Methodology for Solar PV Farms using Hybrid AMH and Deep Learning Techniques
abstract: In this article, an intelligent fault detection mechanism is proposed to classify multiple electrical faults. Various electrical faults like line-line fault, open circuit fault, short circuit faults, and line-to-ground faults are studied in detail. Voltage and current sensors placed at each solar photovoltaic (SPV) array string collect the data during these fault conditions. Machine learning and Deep learning techniques are used to classify the type of fault and can even detect the exact location of the fault. A mismatch detection circuit consisting of a boost converter and optocoupler is designed to differentiate between mismatch faults and electrical faults; this circuit design also indicates the exact location of a mismatch fault. The proposed method is implemented in the Python platform and the results are analysed.

articleTitle: IPMSM Drive System for Electric Vehicle Use FOC with MTPA and FWC Technique
abstract: Electric vehicle motors must exhibit high efficiency, high power density, high torque, and minimal use of magnetic materials, making the interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) an optimal choice. However, achieving maximum torque across the entire operational range is a challenging task. This paper presents a control strategy for IPMSM using field-oriented control (FOC). For operations below the rated speed, the maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) method is applied, while for speeds exceeding the rated level, field weakening control is employed. Moreover, rotor position measurement is enhanced by integrating an adaptive gain mechanism with a complementary filter, effectively mitigating the effects of external disturbances. This results in a system with low steady-state error. The system also incorporates CAN bus communication to facilitate seamless interfacing. The proposed controller was tested on a 13 kW IPMSM. The test results reveal that the control system achieves excellent dynamic response, accurately tracks reference speeds, and maintains minimal steady-state error.

articleTitle: Analysis of Knee Voltage for Organic Diode Fabricated from Sakon Nakhon Indigo
abstract: Indigo plantations are widespread across Sakon Nakhon province, Thailand. The pigment extracted from the indigo plant has the characteristic of being semiconductor. In order to effectively utilize the indigo pigments in the electronic applications, some essential properties of the materials need to be comprehensively investigated. In this study, indigo pigments were produced from fermentation and extraction processes from indigo leaves.
