The obtained indigo pigments were used to fabricate a back-to-back diode, and the measurement of the electrical properties, including voltage and current, resistance, and conductivity have been experimentally investigated. The analytical results showed that the voltage and current characteristics of the indigo pigment exhibited a high knee voltage at 1.5 V of the forward bias while the reverse bias saturation current also exhibited a high value, which was 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> A at reverse bias. The unbalanced waveform was reached because of the surface junction between indigo pigment and different electrode materials with work functions. From resistance and conductivity profiles, the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> period shows the broadest range of high electrical potential bias because of the influence of R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Indigo</inf> <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pigment</inf>, leading to the high knee voltage. Hence, indigo pigment tends to be developed as an organic semiconductor material for high electrical potential bias in commercial electrical devices.

articleTitle: Transcription for Thai Traditional Medicine Texts with Wav2Vec2
abstract: Recently, Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) technology is widely used for communication convenience in converting speech to text. Initial surveys reveal that existing studies on ASR, both in Thai and foreign languages, focus on contemporary language communication, lacking support for specialized vocabulary. Thai Traditional Medicine (TTM) contain ancient medical terminology recorded in various media such as palm leaves, parchment, notebooks, and inscriptions. Centuries of textual preservation have led to text degradation. Given the suitability of ASR study to accommodate medical terminology and ancient languages, it is proposed to apply it to convert original Thai Traditional Medicine texts into contemporary language, aiding experts in reading and interpreting them. ASR involves converting speech signals into text. In this paper, we propose an end-to-end speech recognition approach for Thai Traditional Medical texts leveraging self-supervised learning (SSL) to overcome the limitations of limited labeled data. We utilize a transformer-based model pre-trained (XLSR-Wav2Vec) on unlabeled TTM texts speech data using SSL techniques and fine-tune it with a small dataset of labeled TTM texts audio-text pairs. Due to the absence of a Thai Traditional Medicine vocabulary repository, a dataset comprising text and speech is developed, consisting of 1,800 training sentences and 200 test sentences randomly selected from recordings of 10 Thai Traditional Medicine experts. Offline evaluation methods are employed, resulting in improved accuracy rates. Future efforts will focus on expanding the speech dataset to enhance recognition accuracy further. This study lays the groundwork for efficiently extracting knowledge from Thai Traditional Medicine prescriptions, ensuring the preservation of this valuable heritage for future generations.

articleTitle: Optimized Load-Aware Mechanism for Dynamic CoMP Clustering in Ultra-Dense Networks
abstract: Ultra-Dense Networks (UDN) offer enhanced network performance via a significantly high deployment density of small cells. The system efficiency highly depends on cell coordination using the Coordinated Multipoint (CoMP) techniques. To allow better management of traffic load across cells, the key challenge is the clustering of CoMP-coordinated cells. This article provides an optimized mechanism based on the load-aware concept deployed in the cell clustering mechanism to ensure that the clusters are formed in a way that overloaded cells are fairly and appropriately clustered with available cells i.e. cells that have available resources and can offload heavy traffic from dense cells. The performance of the system has been observed using the system model adapted here compared with our previous work on dynamic CoMP clustering. Major improvements are presented in terms of spectrum efficiency and throughput performance.

articleTitle: The Cascade PI Controller Design for Hydrogen Electric Bike Systems
abstract: The paper presents the cascade PI controller design for a DC/DC converter. The hydrogen is used as the main energy source feeding to the fuel cell stack in which the voltage generated from the fuel cell is fluctuated. As a result, the DC/DC converter is used to regulate the voltage feeding to the electric bike driving systems. The controller design using the standard second order system is proposed. The simulation results from MATLAB/SIMULINK shows that the resulting cascade PI controller can regulate the voltage even the power load level is varied. The considered system with the controller designed by the proposed method can provide the good voltage response until the rated power can be achieved. The ripple voltage in the steady state is under 0.5% following the standard ISO-21780-2020.

articleTitle: Analyzing a Decade Data with Proposed Indexes for HVAC Energy Management of Designated Buildings in Thailand
abstract: This paper presents the analysis of Energy Conservation Measures (ECMs) data of Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems of designated buildings in Thailand to help decisions for applying ECMs in future energy management. Data acquired from annual energy management reports applied to the Department of Alternative Energy Development and Efficiency and used verification methods to enhance the accuracy of annual energy consumption and ECMs, in terms of annual investment, energy saving, and power reduction then calculate indexes to analyze 1. total energy saving, 2. energy saving ratio and 3. investment ratio. Indexes will be used to support further decisions for high-potential ECMs. First of all, the total energy saving from ECMs in Thailand is increasing consistently at 0.98% yearly. From the perspective of processes, Machine change (MC) has the highest proportion at 56.95% of energy saving with 49.61% of distributions of measures. From equipment point of view, split-type air conditioners (Split ACs) and Chillers were high energy saving at 40.66% and 37.15%, respectively. Secondly, the energy saving ratio of Chillers shows that MC process is 4.33 times more effective than Housekeeping (HK). While applying same HK process to Chillers is 2.35 times more effective than Split ACs. Lastly, the investment ratio of Chillers shows that MC requires 15.29 times higher investment than HK to achieve the same power reduction. Moreover, analyzing proposed indexes of designated buildings in this paper shows that if prioritized MC in Chillers will achieve higher energy saving compared to Split ACs while the investment ratio is only 1.77 times higher. In otherwise, from a number of unimplemented ECMs in the designated buildings show that Split ACs has 1.13 times higher potential of the overall energy saving when compared to Chillers. Finally, based on the equipment timelines, MC will require for all equipment by the end. However, considering investment and equipment conditions shows that at some point, HK and PI might be better in specific conditions and times.

articleTitle: Semantic Search Engine, Thai Traditional Medicine Knowledge Graph Application
abstract: In this paper, a semantic information retrieval framework is presented to improve the precision of search results by concentrating on the context of concepts is presented. Instead of the keyword matching technique, the graph theory is used for leveraging the relationships and meanings of search terms. Information is represented as a knowledge graph for semantic searching performed by the inference engine and results are passed to the NLP technique for interpreting entity, relationship and property to their relevancy query. In the current system, we focused on healthcare system to helping the foundation recommendations of Thai Traditional Medicine. Once Thai Traditional Medicine contains a numerous of words which have the same meaning, the traditional keyword based cannot retrieve all relevant document. In our proposed semantic architecture, the query is performed an context-based understanding for retrieving all relevant document, therefore, it can retrieve the same number of documents for the queries which have the same meaning.

articleTitle: Effect of PLL Bandwidth on Stability of Grid-Tied Inverter under Grid Impedance Variations
abstract: The stability of grid-tied inverter (GTI) is a critical concern in microgrid environments, particularly under varying grid conditions where impedance mismatches and control dynamics significantly impact performance. phase-locked loop (PLL) bandwidth emerges as a key parameter influencing GTI stability, as it directly affects the inverter’s output impedance and overall system dynamics. This paper investigates the impact of PLL bandwidth on the stability of an LCL-filtered grid tied inverter (LCL-GTI) using impedance-based stability analysis. A comprehensive small-signal model is developed to derive the output impedance of GTI by considering the power stage, current controller, and PLL dynamics. The stability is evaluated using the generalized Nyquist criterion (GNC) to analyze the system's behavior across different PLL bandwidths. Experimental validation is conducted using a 3.8 kW LCL-GTI, demonstrates the critical influence of PLL bandwidth on GTI stability, offering practical insights for designing robust synchronization mechanisms to enhance GTI reliability in microgrid applications.

articleTitle: Real-time Sorting of Plastic Waste for Pre-Cleaning Recycle
abstract: Despite Thailand’s longstanding efforts in plastic waste sorting, a substantial portion remains unrecycled. This paper introduces an innovative approach utilizing the YOLOv8s deep learning algorithm for real-time plastic waste sorting, specifically targeting five categories: bottles (left and right), glass (left and right), and food containers. The dataset comprises 408 images of everyday plastic waste, including grayscale variations. Our experimental results demonstrate an average F1-score of 85%, precision of 96.6%, precision-recall of 89%, and a confusion matrix showing classification confidence levels of 100% for bottle left and food containers, 87% for bottle right and 86% for glass right.

articleTitle: 2D Polynomial Regression Modeling for Predictive Analysis of Glucose Concentration in NP-Model Fractal Microwave Sensor Using Frequency and Transmission Coefficient Disparities
abstract: The article introduces a two-dimensional polynomial regression model for the predictive analysis of glucose concentration in a fractal microwave sensor NP model, utilizing frequency and transmission coefficient differences to examine their correlation with glucose concentration levels. The sensor employed in this investigation is fabricated on an economical FR-4 substrate to minimize costs. The sensor structure is developed with the fractal structure reduction method established by the NP model to operate at a frequency of roughly 2.97 GHz. The CST Studio software is utilized to analyze the findings from the simulation of the suggested sensor structure. Furthermore, the proposed sensor is integrated into a test apparatus comprising a sensor platform and a liquid tube constructed from PPA material. The liquid under examination is a glucose and water mixture at varying concentrations. It was analyzed using a VNA instrument to evaluate its frequency response and the magnitude of the alteration in the transmission coefficient. The values are utilized to create a two-dimensional polynomial regression model. The experiments demonstrated that the proposed sensor model possesses an Adjusted R² value of 0.99499 and an average error of approximately 3.57% for glucose concentration analysis throughout the range of 5% to 30%, with sensitivities of 0.00879 dB/% for insertion loss and 0.092 MHz/% for frequency variation, facilitating accurate glucose concentration prediction analysis.

articleTitle: Efficiency Analysis of Adaptive Sequentially Weighted Median Filter (ASWMF) For Greatly Distorted Impulse Noise
abstract: On this noise destruction community, unusually the settle intensity impulsive noise (SIIN), the most recent noise destruction mechanism, which is broadly expressed by noise tracking-down mechanism and noise destruction mechanism, is an inescapable precedent mechanism that must be prosecuted in advance of the other perplex image processing mechanisms. The first contribution of this research work is the analysis determination of the max extreme number, which make the ASWMF mechanism the greatest efficiency for all-percentage noise propagation. By the precedent result (the optimal max extreme number), the second contribution of this research work is the analysis efficiency of the ASWMF mechanism for all-percentage noise propagation. The experiment section situationally analyzes the efficiency of the ASWMF noise destruction mechanism, which is one of the most recent noise destruction mechanisms, in comparison with other precedent noise destruction mechanisms like MF, SMF, and AMF for destructing the settle intensity impulsive noise (SIIN). In the 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> experimental analysis, plentiful corrupted portraitures, which are expressed of Girl, Lena and Pepper for all-percentage noise propagation, are examined by the noise destruction mechanism rested on ASWMF in order to estimate the optimal max extreme number for providing the greatest efficiency of the noise destruction perspective. In the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> experimental analysis, these corrupted portraitures are examined by the noise destruction mechanism rested on ASWMF, which is differentiate with other precedent noise destruction mechanisms like MF, SMF, and AMF.

articleTitle: Study of magnetic saturation in a boost converter: modeling and nonlinear control
abstract: This paper investigates a large-signal model for a boost DC-DC converter with a nonlinear controller, considering the nonlinear magnetic characteristics of the inductor that might affect system stability. The converter is designed with an optimized inductor core for space-constrained applications where output voltage quality is less critical, such as wind turbine kites and wave energy generators. Traditional linear controllers may underperform due to inductor nonlinearity. This study investigates the impact of magnetic saturation on the system's performances using a trajectory controller and shows that neglecting these effects degrades control performance. Under unmatched conditions on inductance’s value, the eigenvalues of the controlled system change. The simulation results align with the system's eigenvalues by explicitly incorporating the inductor's nonlinear characteristics, confirming the model's accuracy.

articleTitle: Pilot-Aided Channel Estimation for 4×4 MIMO-OFDM in Multi-Gigabit Wireless Communication Systems
abstract: This paper investigates channel estimation techniques and equalization using singular value decomposition for 4 × 4 multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing systems employed in multi-gigabit wireless communication systems. To achieve high spectral efficiency, the system utilizes spatial multiplexing with independent data streams transmitted on each antenna and employs high-order quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM), such as 1024-QAM and 4096-QAM. The study explores various pilot symbol placement strategies and robust estimation algorithms, including least squares. The pilot-based channel matrix learning with average to minimize noise is proposed. The system numerical simulation performance shows that the proposed method provides a high accuracy of channel matrix estimation. The mean squared error below 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> can be achieved. Additionally, the proposed method is very simple and can be implemented in hardware.

articleTitle: Smart Railway Cross section Module by Perspective Transformations with an ECTS-Level 1 Approach
abstract: This paper propose an innovation design of the smart railway cross section module that was based on geometric transformations approach and ECTS level 1 control. Meanwhile the aim of this research expect to develop the overall of an automatic railway cross section on the road paradigm shift with an engineering design methods. The concept of module design was generated here according with the digital transformation platform to enhance of smart railway cross section requirements meet the need of approaching smart city policy of Thailand 4.0. The geometric transformation can specify object modelling operations both for local coordinate system such as modeling coordinates in this paper and a global coordinate system as a worldwide coordinates in the transportation. With cloud communicating paradigm shift, the new era of the stage of the art design of infrastructure of programmable logic controller (PLC) system to enhance the computing resources with a long distance remote control and served them as a service on demand with highly resolutions transportation system that comes with service level agreement (SLA) as fidelity with less waiting time. While the fuzzy-proportional plus integral control (F-PI) was modified with fuzzy ladder scheme of PLC for enhancing their ability, capability and utility of the overall system performance such as dynamic loading effect management in the real time. The simulations results were several tested with the modelling design methodology, while the real prototype module was also several tested in the laboratory room that should be satisfied with design concept. The overall performance criteria will be adjusted again until suitable to use in practical usage and stable.

articleTitle: EIS-Based Technique for SOH Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: This paper explores the application of Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) for assessing the State of Health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), with Coulomb Counting used as a reference for validation. EIS offers a non-destructive method to evaluate impedance and provides insights into parameters like charge transfer resistance (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ct</inf>), which correlates with SOH. Experimental results reveal a clear link between R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ct</inf> and SOH, with fractional-order models (FOM) enhancing accuracy in capturing real-world battery complexities. Tests on five LIB cells demonstrated a strong correlation between EIS-based SOH estimations and reference values from Coulomb Counting, with minor deviations attributed to measurement errors and battery degradation. This study underscores the reliability of EIS for battery diagnostics and its potential for energy storage applications.

articleTitle: The Performance Study on CoAP Protocol over an OpenThread Network
abstract: Smart homes, smart logistics, healthcare, smart agriculture, and other industries have extensively utilized the Internet of Things (IoT) in recent years. Their ability to communicate data across devices through the Internet has significantly facilitated their increasing popularity. The utilization of IoT devices is anticipated to expand in the future owing to advancements in associated technologies and the increasing demand for more intelligent and efficient systems. The need for IoT technology has led to the introduction of protocols like CoAP, 6LowPAN, and Thread to accommodate the increasing proliferation of IoT devices. However, the increasing number of IoT devices makes network congestion a critical concern. Therefore, in our study, we concentrate on addressing traffic congestion in a real-world setting, utilizing the popular nRF52840 modules. The study shows that nodes transmit data at a rate exceeding 150 packets per second, resulting in over 50% packet loss, an increase in round trip time (RTT), and an increase in retransmission packets as the number of nodes increases.

articleTitle: Operational Efficiency of Synchronous Reluctance Generator Systems using Vector Control
abstract: This study aims to verify the operation of a system that combines a generator, an inverter to control it, and a power conditioner, as well as to observe the system efficiency at the theoretical MTPA (Maximum Torque Per Ampere) point. The generator is driven by vector control with a rated output of 12 kW, and the inverter has a capacity of 47 kW.

articleTitle: A Novel 3-Phase Series AC Cap-CSI-Buck Grid-tied PV Transformerless Inverter with Low Grid Voltage Fault Ride-Through Capacity
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) cells operate at their maximum power point (MPPT) when their terminal voltage is 75-85% of the open-circuit voltage, creating design challenges for grid-tied PV inverters. These inverters must handle maximum voltage stresses while maintaining efficiency at lower MPPT voltages and comply with grid-fault voltage drop requirements. Current solutions require additional voltage regulators or low voltage fault ride-through (LVFRT) units, increasing cost, complexity, and power losses. This paper proposes a novel 3-phase grid-tied PV transformerless inverter topology combining series AC capacitors, current source inverter (CSI), and a buck converter. This design enables large voltage regulation and voltage drop without additional units. Simulated and experimental results validate its feasibility, demonstrating improved efficiency and voltage drop performance under various grid faults and solar conditions compared to traditional CSI designs.

articleTitle: Backstepping control for a boost converter
abstract: The paper presents an application of a backstepping method to control a boost converter operating in a continuous current conduction mode, and there are two differential equations for the inductor current and output capacitor voltage describing the boost converter. A proposed control law for both current and voltage loops is presented. The main advantage of this control method is that it uses a scalar equation instead of a vector, unlike nonlinear control methods. The simulation results are given to validate the control method.

articleTitle: Aquaponic System with IoT for Sustainable Farming
abstract: Aquaponics is an innovative agricultural approach that combines aquaculture (fish farming) and hydroponics (soilless plant cultivation) into a closed-loop ecosystem. This system leverages the natural synergy between fish and plants, where nutrient-rich water from the fish tank supports plant growth. In contrast, plants naturally filter and purify the water for the fish. The project integrates IoT technology, enabling automation and real-time monitoring of essential parameters such as water levels, temperature, and system operation through the Blynk application. The designed aquaponics system demonstrates a scalable and efficient solution suitable for limited spaces, such as urban areas. It promotes sustainable agriculture by reducing water usage and optimizing resource management. Initial experiments show promising results, highlighting the system's potential for improving plant growth rates and overall efficiency in food production.

articleTitle: Development of Charge Integrator Circuits with a Microcontroller for Cylindrical Capacitive Sensors in Paddy Moisture Balance Detectors
abstract: This article presents a method for indirectly measuring the moisture content of paddy using a cylindrical capacitive sensor combined with Charge Integrator Circuits. The moisture measurement device operates based on the principle of the dielectric constant of paddy, which changes according to the moisture content within them. The system consists of a moisture detection section utilizing a cylindrical capacitor, a signal generator operating at a frequency of 500 Hz with a microcontroller, a signal conditioning circuit converting the signal to voltage, and a processing unit. Testing was conducted with paddy at five different moisture levels, demonstrating the ability to accurately determine the moisture content of the rice. When compared to the commercially available PM-450TH moisture meter, the results showed a linear response across the measurement range, with an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value of 0.9824 and an average error of 2.6%. This technology has the potential for further development and application to other types of seeds in the future.

articleTitle: Partial Shading Detection Technique Development for a Photovoltaic Array
abstract: This study introduces an approach for detecting partial shading on a photovoltaic array, designed to reduce unnecessary voltage scanning during maximum power point tracking under consistent sunlight conditions. The method leverages the linear relationship between the maximum power point current and the short-circuit current of the array, as well as the correlation between the maximum power point conductance and the conductance calculated from the ratio of short-circuit current to open-circuit voltage. By employing this technique, the controller can promptly identify instances of partial shading as soon as the first maximum power point is located, enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of the tracking process.

articleTitle: Heart Sound Segmentation using Envelogram in Hadamard Domain
abstract: A new framework for heart sound segmentation is proposed. The segmentation algorithm is based on the envelope created using the energy of the first component of the transformed signal, which intensifies the first and second heart sound while attenuating the effects of noise and murmur. Based on the created envelogram, a threshold is calculated to eliminate the effects of noise and low-intensity signals. The estimation of cardiac cycle length using statistical characteristics of the envelope signal is developed. Finally, individual cardiac cycles are extracted from the heart sound. The proposed method showed promising results and high robustness across a wide range of heart sounds.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Reflection-Transmission Surface for Dual-Beam Direction and Angular Control in mmWave Systems
abstract: A reconfigurable reflection-transmission surface (RRTS) is proposed for dual-beam direction and angular control in millimeter-wave (mmWave) systems. The RRTS element is designed to operate within the frequency range of 23.9 to 27.7 GHz for reflection mode and 22.8 to 29.0 GHz for transmission mode, corresponding to the 26 GHz mmWave band (n258: 24.25-27.5 GHz). The element consists of a copper hexagonal ring structure on the top layer and a hexagonal patch on the bottom layer. Two p-i-n diodes are integrated into the design to electronically control the 180° phase difference of each mode. A 10 × 20 array of RRTS elements is designed and analyzed. The results demonstrate that the proposed RRTS enables reconfigurable operation in reflection (backward space), transmission (forward space), and hybrid (full space) modes, utilizing different periodic coding sequences to allow precise control over dual beams, enabling independent steering and scanning. The beam deviation error is found to be less than ±1.6° for both reflection and transmission modes, and less than ±5° for the hybrid mode, as compared to theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Data-Driven Modeling for Day-Ahead Solar Power Forecasting: A Case Study of the SUT Campus Floating Solar System
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of forecasting methods for solar PV power generation, using a two-step forecasting approach. The data includes solar irradiance, global tilted irradiance, temperature, humidity, and wind speed, analyzed with LSTM, Bi-LSTM, GRU, and RF models, 7,665 samples of 30-minute recordings from 2023. In the first part of the study, the important factors affecting power generation, irradiance and temperature, are forecasted using the LSTM method to consider the relationship between external factors and power generation. In the second part of the study, the results from the aforementioned forecasting are used to predict power generation. The forecast results obtained by LSTM, Bi-LSTM, GRU, and RF, were investigated and compared. This study not only helps to better understand the relationship between external factors and power generation but also significantly improves the overall forecasting efficiency.

articleTitle: The Integrating Mini PLC FX1N with Raspberry Pi for Prototyping of Industrial Control
abstract: In contemporary industries, machine languages have become essential for producing various products and services. Ladder Logic is a prominent programming language commonly utilized in different sectors, including web development, software engineering, data science, and machine learning. Conversely, C and C++ are versatile programming languages that support object-oriented and procedural programming paradigms and effective memory management. These languages find applications in diverse fields, such as embedded systems and ladder programming, where ladder logic diagrams represent machinery control systems. Programmers must possess a comprehensive understanding of system operations and effectively use a variety of symbols to indicate specific functions to create a ladder diagram accurately. Tasks involving Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) typically require computer and communication software, such as the Raspberry Pi Pico microcontroller board. GX Works2 is a PLC software application that facilitates the testing and simulation of different three-phase motor circuits, thereby enabling precise control of actual power equipment. This article describes programming hardware control systems with Ladder language. This language is crucial for coding Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), widely used in industrial plants.

articleTitle: Computer Vision in Robotic Zen Garden Systems: An Embedded Approach for Contour Detection and Pattern Generation
abstract: This paper presents an integrated system that combines computer vision and robotics to automate the creation of traditional Zen garden patterns. The system uses a single Raspberry Pi to detect contours in real time and generate aesthetically pleasing patterns around them, mimicking natural elements like water ripples and waves. By leveraging OpenCV for contour detection and custom pattern generation algorithms, the system produces dynamic, high-quality designs based on the placement and different sizes and shapes of objects within the garden. The experimental results of this system include high detection accuracy, with precision and recall rates exceeding 90% for object classification, and the ability to generate smooth, fluid patterns that closely align with traditional Zen garden aesthetics. Furthermore, the system demonstrates robust real-time performance and ensures seamless motor control. This paper showcases a cost-effective and efficient solution for blending robotics with creative automation in Zen garden design.

articleTitle: Development of an Autonomous EV Navigation System Using Instance Segmentation for Medical Supply Delivery
abstract: This paper describes an approach for using instance segmentation techniques to create an autonomous navigation system for driverless electric vehicles (EVs). To replace conventional transportation methods that mostly depend on human drivers, the main goal is to move medical supplies between buildings in the Suranaree University of Technology (SUT) Hospital region. Five primary components comprise the development of the EV-based medical supply transport system: i) the steering and drive systems; ii) autonomous navigation and obstacle detection systems; iii) instance segmentation techniques; iv) RP lidar for obstacle detection; and v) the EV working algorithm. The test route is designed to cover 525 m from a starting point to an endpoint, with a speed range of 0 to 1.5 m/s for the EV performed in this study. The EV will come to a turn left at 251 and 335 m along this path and a turn right at 293 m. In the instance segmentation autonomous navigation test, the EV maintained an average speed of 0.99 m/s and an average power usage of 0.22 kW while driving in a straight line. However, the EV's speed and power consumption decreased to zero to enable directional corrections when it encountered turns, including a turn right at 293 m and turns left at 251 m and 335 m. As a result, the EV was able to complete the required turns and proceed straight ahead until it reached the destination.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Antenna Gain With M&W Slot Model on EBG Reflector Structure Utilizing Reflection Phase Diagram Analysis
abstract: This research demonstrates the improvement in antenna gain by utilizing an EBG reflector. The EBG reflector includes a unit cell with grooves shaped like the letters M and W to mitigate surface waves at a frequency of 2.45 GHz. The suggested EBG reflector is constructed on an FR-4 substrate exhibiting a uniform dielectric constant of 4.3, a loss tangent of 0.025, and a thickness of 1.6 mm. Furthermore, the impact of boosting the antenna gain can be analyzed by the reflection phase diagram, which exhibits values ranging from +90° to -90° at the resonant frequency of the reflector. The proposed EBG reflector comprises 5x5 unit cells. The testing results of the reflector's performance, when integrated with a general dipole antenna, indicate that it can effectively respond to the resonant frequency of 2.45 GHz, with a |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| level below -10 dB within the frequency range of 2.2 GHz to 2.6 GHz, thereby adequately covering the IEEE 802.11 b/g/n band. The suggested EBG reflector exhibits a gain of around 6.5 dBi at 2.45 GHz, indicating its efficacy in enhancing gain relative to the standard PEC reflector. Moreover, the radiation pattern is also directional.

articleTitle: Implement an acoustic sound system by Hann Window with Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to analyze characteristics in a pipe for robotic
abstract: By measuring the amplitude utilizing the pipe's frequency range, we create an acoustic sound system to test in a pipe. In this study, we use digital signal processing techniques with a microphone to be a part of sensors. Our primary objective is to transmit signals from a loudspeaker or sender to the microphone or receiver while minimizing external noise and managing acoustic dispersion within the pipe. We develop an acoustic system based on pipes that can be applied to robotics in the future. Using a microphone and loudspeaker, we suggest the characteristics of the acoustic sound in the pipe. This subject is covered by the large field of acoustic signal processing. Our project intends to bring about a significant change in the management of buried pipe infrastructure in the future by developing specialized robots that can operate within subterranean pipe networks for communication. The assessment of acoustics in pipes using acoustic sound analysis is the focus of our research.

articleTitle: Optimal Coordination of Adaptive Overcurrent Relay for Microgrid System Using Hybrid PSO-LP
abstract: This paper specializes on determining of optimal overcurrent relay coordination, which is imperative for primary and backup overcurrent relays using hybrid particle swam optimization (PSO) and linear programing (LP). Inspection is conducted on a 4-bus radial system connected to distributed energy resources (DER). The pick-up current is determined using PSO, meanwhile the time multiplier setting (TMS) is determined by LP, to solve the overcurrent relay (OCR) coordination problem. The results demonstrate a significant reduction in relay operating time, showing improved efficiency compared to conventional methods.

articleTitle: Soft Starting of a Modified Three-Phase Induction Motor with a Single-Phase Synchronous PWM AC Chopper
abstract: This paper presents a soft starting method for a modified three-phase induction motor using a single-phase synchronous PWM AC chopper to reduce starting current and electromagnetic torque pulsation. The modified motor functions as a single-phase induction motor due to the lack of a three-phase source and employs an appropriate capacitor. The synchronous single-phase PWM AC chopper provides several benefits over traditional thyristor soft starters, including a linear relationship between fundamental voltage and modulation index, improved voltage control, and lower harmonic currents. A cost-effective microcontroller gradually increases the duty cycle to create PWM signals for soft starting, achieving nearly a 65% reduction in starting current compared to direct online starting. Simulation and experimental results confirm enhanced starting performance, making it suitable for applications such as water and air pumps.

Author Keywords: Modified three-phase induction motor for a single-phase supply

articleTitle: A Varactor-Based and Dual-Polarized Reconfigurable Reflectarray with 2-Bit Phase Resolution
abstract: A varactor-based 2-bit dual linear-polarized reconfigurable reflectarray (RRA) is presented, featuring a unit cell with a cross-shaped structure on the top layer and a ground plane on the bottom layer. Each unit cell includes two orthogonally arranged varactors, independently biased via bias vias to generate different reflection phase shifts. Four distinct phase states are used to achieve a 2-bit phase resolution. A 16 × 16 unit cell RRA is designed and analyzed, showing that it can achieve ±60º beam steering for both linear polarizations. The maximum gain is 16.65 dBi at broadside, with cross-polarization levels below -14 dB. As the beam scans away from broadside, the gain decreases approximately as cos(θ). Compared to a 1-bit configuration, the proposed 2-bit RRA shows improved performance in gain, sidelobe levels, and beam direction accuracy.

articleTitle: Electronically Tunable VDCC-Based Third-Order Quadrature Oscillator
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of a third-order quadrature oscillator using Voltage Differencing Current Conveyors (VDCCs). The proposed circuit generates stable quadrature outputs with a 90-degree phase difference at a target frequency of approximately 106kHz where the THD drops to approximately 1.2. PSPICE simulations were conducted to validate the oscillator's performance, demonstrating steady-state behavior, consistent amplitude, and minimal harmonic distortion. The design’s electronic tunability, achieved by adjusting bias currents, enables precise frequency control, making it suitable for applications in signal processing and communications. The simulation results confirm the oscillator's potential for integration into modern electronic systems requiring reliable, low-distortion quadrature signals.

articleTitle: Investigations of a Circularly Polarized Slotted Corner-Truncated Microstrip Patch Antenna with Split-Ring AMC Reflector
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a circularly polarized slotted corner-truncated microstrip patch antenna integrated with a split-ring artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) metasurface for WLAN applications at 2.45 GHz. The antenna design incorporates structural adaptations, such as slotted apertures and corner truncations, to enhance impedance matching and achieve circular polarization. To further improve performance, a split-ring AMC metasurface was employed, resulting in enhanced polarization purity and bandwidth. The proposed design achieves an impedance bandwidth (|S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| below −10 dB) from 2.33 GHz to 2.75 GHz and an axial ratio (AR) below 3 dB over the frequency range of 2.40 GHz to 2.55 GHz, and a peak gain of approximately 4.40 dBic at 2.45 GHz. Simulated results are validated by measured results of the fabricated prototype, demonstrating close agreement and confirming the robustness of the design methodology. This work highlights an innovative approach to compact and high-performance antenna design, ensuring its suitability for modern WLAN communication systems.

articleTitle: A Study on the Modeling of ATP Depletion in Cardiac Muscle Cells Induced by Solar Proton Flux Using Differential Equations and Its Potential to Explain Sudden Unexpected Nocturnal Death Syndrome (SUNDS) in Thailand
abstract: This study models the dynamics of ATP depletion and reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation in cardiac muscle cells under the influence of solar proton flux (SPF), focusing on both healthy individuals and heart disease patients. Using differential equations, the concentrations of ATP and ROS were simulated over a 24-hour period. In healthy individuals, ATP levels gradually decreased due to ROS-induced damage, with ROS concentrations peaking at the end of the 24-hour period. In contrast, heart disease patients, who started with lower ATP levels, experienced a faster depletion of ATP and a more rapid increase in ROS, indicating higher oxidative stress. These results demonstrated that solar proton flux exacerbates oxidative damage in cardiac cells. This effect is particularly pronounced in individuals with pre-existing heart conditions. This may link to another theory explaining Sudden Unexpected Nocturnal Death Syndrome (SUNDS) in Thailand. The study provides valuable insights into the potential effects of solar activity on heart health—especially in those with cardiovascular diseases. It also underscores the importance of maintaining ATP homeostasis in cardiac cells and calls for further research on therapeutic strategies to mitigate oxidative damage in the future.

articleTitle: A Comparative Life Cycle Greenhouse Gas Emission Analysis of BEV, PHEV, HEV and ICEV in Thailand
abstract: This research conducts a well-to-wheel (WTW) assessment to analyze greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from Battery Electric Vehicle (BEV), Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle (PHEV), Hybrid Electric Vehicle (HEV), and Internal Combustion Engine Vehicle (ICEV). To analyze and compare the greenhouse gas emissions of electric vehicles (EVs) with those of traditional vehicles, four car models from different brands were selected within the subcompact passenger car category, featuring a driving power output between 90 and 100 horsepower. The findings highlighted that BEV exhibits a substantial reduction of over 46% in WTW GHG emissions when compared with ICEV. The results further revealed that GHG emissions from the well-to-tank (WTT) process are lowest for ICEV and highest for BEV, with the disparity due to varying fossil fuel consumption across fuel production processes. Contrary, the tank-to-wheel (TTW) process contributes significantly to greenhouse gas emissions in ICEV and HEV, while it has a minor impact on PHEV, primarily due to gasoline combustion. In addition, the WTW GHG emissions of electric vehicles can be further reduced by increasing the share of renewable energy in the electricity generation mix. These insights hold valuable implications for future research on emissions in the transportation sector and offer a basis for evaluating the effectiveness of carbon neutrality policies in Thailand.

articleTitle: Conceivable Design of a Wideband Unidirectional Antenna using Truncated Microstrip Patches for S-Band Applications
abstract: This paper presents the conceivable design of a wideband unidirectional antenna suitable for CubeSat applications operating in the S-band frequency ranges of 2.025-2.110 GHz (uplink band) and 2.200-2.290 GHz (downlink band). The antenna employs a truncated microstrip patch design combined with additional parasitic patches to achieve circular polarization. It is printed on an RT/duroid<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> 5880 substrate with a thickness of 0.6 mm and a relative permittivity of 2.2. The design consists of a central truncated radiating patch and four segment-circular parasitic patches, positioned near the edges of the substrate to enhance bandwidth and axial ratio performance, which is crucial for achieving circular polarization. The antenna is excited using a coaxial probe feed to ensure efficient energy transfer and proper impedance matching. Simulation results demonstrate that the antenna achieves a wide impedance bandwidth covering 1.80 GHz to 2.40 GHz with a reflection coefficient (|S11|) below -10 dB. The axial ratio remains below 3 dB across the frequency range of 2.025 GHz to 2.290 GHz, confirming circular polarization, with a minimum axial ratio of 1.34 dB at 2.25 GHz. Additionally, the antenna exhibits a stable gain of approximately 7.28 dBic at 2.15 GHz, making it suitable for CubeSat communication systems requiring reliable and efficient signal transmission. To further strengthen the contribution of this research, a performance comparison with existing CubeSat antennas is provided, along with a discussion of potential environmental impacts in space, such as temperature variations and radiation effects. Future work will focus on prototyping, experimental validation, and optimizing the antenna design for different mission scenarios, including scaling for other frequency bands and multi-antenna configurations.

articleTitle: Deep Learning based Classification of Depression and Suicidal Risk Among Normal Speakers using Delta-Spectral Cepstral Coefficients
abstract: This study utilizes deep learning techniques to develop a precise model for identifying audio recordings, of female speakers for their mental health conditions. The female speakers were categorized into three volunteer groups, which are remitted (RMT), depressed ( DPR), and high-risk suicidal (HRK) by psychiatrist. The various deep learning techniques such as CNN1D, CNN2D, SVM and LSTM were thoroughly trained and validated with our feature samples which are the Delta MFCC (∆MFCC), representing the vocal-tract frequency response associated with different categorized emotional illnesses of three studied volunteer groups. The experimental results show that the CNN2D model achieved the highest accuracies of 0.95 and 0.99 among studied models in classifying ∆MFCC samples between RMT and DPR groups, and between RMT and HRK groups, respectively. Moreover, precision and recall scores were also robust for the CNN models. In contrast, the SVM model achieved with accuracy of 0.83 as compare to CNN models while its precision and recall found to be adequately high. The findings can significantly contribute to understanding of affected vocal characteristics of spoken sound samples associated with mental illness conditions.

articleTitle: Strategies for Reducing Carbon Emissions Through Effective Transportation Management
abstract: This paper explores innovative strategies for reducing carbon emissions through improved logistics transport management practices. Using real-world data, the study identifies inefficiencies in fuel use, suboptimal vehicle speed, and tire pressure, and presents actionable recommendations such as load optimization, speed policy, and preventive maintenance practice, without investment in fleet upgrading or adoption of renewable energy. The findings demonstrate significant reductions in GHG emissions while maintaining operational efficiency, providing a scalable model for sustainable logistics.

articleTitle: An Implementation of the MST-SMC BLDC for Virtual Haptic
abstract: This paper presents the design, implementation, and experimentation of a virtual haptic system, allowing the user to feel physical forces from the operating area. The system includes a BLDC motor control side and an operating area side. Each BLDC motor is equipped with a control board containing a three-phase inverter, microcontroller, magnetic encoder, and CAN transceiver. Experimental results demonstrated that both motor systems could rotate precisely in synchronization, with a maximum error of 0.3 rad. The virtual torque reflection on the control side differed by 13.3% compared to the torque on the operating area side.

articleTitle: Design of Monopole Transparent Antenna for Satellite Internet Aboard Aircraft
abstract: This research presents the design of a transparent antenna for satellite internet aboard aircraft. The presented antenna comprises a triangular arrow monopole antenna fed by a tapered microstrip transmission line. It employs a polycarbonate composite substrate with a dielectric constant (εr) of 2.8 and a thickness (h) of 1 mm. The proposed transparent antenna achieves a bandwidth in the frequency range of 10.42–22.70 GHz, with an omnidirectional radiation pattern and an average gain of 2.57 dBi, effectively covering the Ku band for satellite internet applications. The antenna design was simulated using electromagnetic wave CST simulation software, and a prototype antenna was fabricated. The designed antenna exhibits a reflection coefficient of less than -10 dB throughout the 10.7–12.7 GHz frequency range, which is the operational frequency range for satellite internet and is an acceptable value in research terms. Moreover, a conductor with a thickness of 0.035 mm sits on a composite substrate material to form the antenna structure for satellite internet aboard aircraft. We need to study and apply various techniques to further enhance the antenna's performance in future designs.

articleTitle: Comparison of Unsupervised Learning Algorithms for K-Means Clustering Efficiency in IoE Sensor Detection Systems for Smart Agriculture
abstract: This study investigates the application of clustering algorithms to data collected from color sensors providing frequency signals during the cultivation process. Continuous sampling allowed for real-time data collection, and variations in temperature and humidity were observed to influence signal reception. The dataset's large volume and varying sample sizes necessitated the evaluation of several clustering models for efficient data processing. The experiment tested K-Means, K-Means++, Mini-Batch K-Means, and Bisecting K-Means algorithms. The results reveal that the computation time for each model increased with the number of groups. Specifically, the K-Means, K-Means++, and Mini-Batch K-Means models exhibited shorter computation times, ranging from 0.02 to 0.03 seconds for two-group scenarios, while the Bisecting K-Means algorithm took significantly longer, approximately 0.10 seconds. Despite the variation in processing times, all models performed similarly in terms of clustering quality, with an average Silhouette Score of 0.82. This score indicates that the algorithms effectively separated data points into well-defined groups while maintaining high accuracy in clustering. Additionally, the analysis highlighted the importance of balancing computation time and clustering quality, particularly as the number of clusters increases. These findings suggest that while computational efficiency may vary across models, the clustering quality remains robust, providing valuable insights for data analysis in agricultural sensor networks. The study's results demonstrate that each clustering model is capable of handling large datasets with high accuracy in grouping, making them applicable to real-world agricultural data processing scenarios. In conclusion, the experiment confirms that all tested models, despite differing in computation time, successfully partitioned the data with high-quality results, offering promising applications for data analysis and optimization in agriculture and sensor-based systems.

articleTitle: Analyzing Appliance Status in Small Residences Through Smart Meter Data
abstract: A smart meter in a small residential area is a valuable device that can analyze energy consumption in attributes. This study presents an analysis and experimental results that focus on analyzing the operating status of each small residential appliance using data from smart meters installed in small residential buildings. This method involves collecting the power (P) and power factor (PF) measurements of electrical appliances obtained from these smart meters, which are then converted into active power (P) and reactive power (Q) for use in determining the type of individual electrical appliances. Modular search tables and other techniques are used to analyze the status of electrical appliances. It emphasizes the simplicity of calculation and the size of the search table suitable for applying microcontrollers in smart meters. This work compares an experimental analysis of complete and modular search tables and a multi-entry conditional search for different types of residential appliances, indicating the differences in use and limitations. According to the experimental analysis, the use of multi-tables significantly reduces the amount of data space compared to the use of full search tables, and the use of multi-tables requires multi-point searches to increase productivity.

articleTitle: Closing Time Analysis of Electromagnetic Relay in Real Time Gas HV Circuit Breaker Simulator
abstract: Developing process of Point-on-Wave Switching Controller, capacitor bank switching is required for testing. While a Real-time simulator is another option for testing, its high cost can be a significant drawback. Therefore, employing a low voltage analog model with real-time circuit breaker simulator becomes a more economical choice. Real-time circuit breaker simulator, which is based on a low-cost microprocessor, can replicate high voltage characteristics, such as gas insulator breakdown and the rate of decrease of dielectric strength (RDDS). To function effectively, this circuit breaker simulator requires a fast-closing, high precision, and low uncertainty switching device. Electromagnetic relays are one potential option for the switching device. As a result, many relays are tested under various closing time conditions, including the first operation after a long idle period and after numerous operational cycles.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electrical Energy Consumption Efficiency Trends, Case Study: A Textile Industry
abstract: The use of electricity in the textile industry tends to increase according to the increasing demand for consumers and products in line with the times, resulting in higher energy consumption and production costs. The CUSUM (Cumulative Sum) chart analysis of electrical energy consumption can accurately detect abnormalities, small changes, or savings in average energy efficiency. This research presents an analysis of the trend of electricity efficiency, using a case study of the textile industry and 24 months of production volume and electrical energy consumption data. These data are analyzed using the CUSUM to investigate energy consumption behavior, along with data from the textile industry. It was found that in the 24-month period, using a linear equation to show the slope of the electrical energy consumption and production volume data, the productive energy consumption (PEC) is 36.136 kWh, and the unproductive energy consumption (UEC) is 200,977 kWh. The UEC is higher than the PEC, such as Use all LED bulbs, turn on and off the switch when not in use, maintain regularly, balance the phase, reduce unnecessary bulb wattage, replace the old air conditioner with a new set of high energy efficiency (EER), use high efficiency motors, and change to a high efficiency air pump. In the subsequent year, various measures were implemented to reduce or conserve energy, leading to a PEC value of 39.31 kWh and a UEC value of 195,855 kWh, resulting in a 23.87% energy savings. Therefore, using CUSUM to analyze the trend of electrical energy efficiency can help plan for future electrical energy usage and be more efficient.

articleTitle: The Impact of Contaminant Particles on the AC Breakdown Voltage of Transformer Oil Mixed with TiO2 Nanoparticles
abstract: Contaminants have huge influences on withstand voltage of transformer oil. Contaminant particles caused by electrical stress and internal mechanisms of transformers affect oil quality, which directly affects insulating ability afterwards. So far, there have been only a few research studies on impacts of contaminants while nanoparticles have recently gained more interest among people in terms of mixing those particles with of transformer oil to increase much better efficiency of transformer insulators. This research mainly focused on 20 μm cellulose-based contaminants in transformer oil and the one mixed with TiO2 nanoparticles at 0.01% concentration of transformer oil volume. Then, they were compared with 4 samples of regular oil. Next, electrical properties were studied by testing the AC breakdown voltage in order to assess quality of liquid insulators in accordance with ASTM D877. The testing results indicated that in case of no contamination, transformer oil mixed with TiO2 nanoparticles contained significantly better withstand voltage than regular transformer oil. This implied higher insulation efficiency nanoparticles were added into transformer oil. Furthermore, in case of cellulose-based contaminants, the testing results also revealed transformer oil mixed with TiO2 nanoparticles contained better withstand voltage than regular transformer oil with cellulose-based contaminants. This implied that nanoparticles could reduce the impact of contamination on insulation of transformer oil.

articleTitle: Development of an IoT-Based Water Pumping Management System for Rice Fields
abstract: Efficient water management is essential for rice cultivation. This requires a large amount of water resources to keep the plants healthy and have maximum yields. Traditional pumping methods, which rely on manual monitoring and control, are time-consuming and often result in water waste and potential equipment theft. This paper proposes the development of an IoT-based automated pumping management system specifically designed to support farmers who grow rice. The system uses an ESP32 microcontroller, a 3-level water level sensor, and a GPS module for real-time water level monitoring and pump control. Notifications are included with the LINE application, allowing farmers to be notified about the water level and location of the pump, thereby reducing the risk of theft. The experimental results found high accuracy in water level monitoring and pump control, with a 100% success rate in preventing overflow and reducing wasteful water consumption. This system provides a reliable and resource-efficient solution for remote water management in the agricultural sector. This helps to increase the sustainability of water use for rice cultivation.

articleTitle: A Feasibility Study of RF Absorption Property of Anti-Static Foam
abstract: This paper presents a test of the power absorption properties of anti-static foam in the frequency range of 600 MHz to 6 GHz for use in small-sized radio frequency anechoic chambers. The test was conducted by placing log-periodic transmit-receive antennas in a standard anechoic chamber, which are employed to generate and measure signals using a vector network analyzer in the form of the S21 parameter. A comparative test was performed under two conditions: (1) measuring signal transmission between the antennas without any obstruction, and (2) placing 1, 2, and 3 layers of anti-static foam between the antennas. The test results demonstrated the power absorption capabilities of the anti-static foam within the frequency range of interest. However, due to the limited size of the square anti-static foam plates, the results in some frequency ranges were not consistent as expected.

articleTitle: Comparison of Reduced-Length FFT-Based Feature for Induction Motor Fault Classification
abstract: This research presents a comparison of FFT-based features which can be used for classifying induction motor faults via neural network. In this paper, the misalignment and rotor bar damage faults are investigated by using stator current as input data only. As the length of the full FFT can include both informative data corresponding to the faults and uninformative data such as noise from environment or electrical supply, only relevant magnitude from FFT bins should be selected and used instead. This paper proposed to use threshold level determined from the magnitude of FFT bins in dataset as a criterion for the selection. From experimental results, an input feature vector created by proposed method can create short input feature vector length to be used by neural network efficiently. The trained neural network performs classification task at 99.98% in accuracy. Comparing to using dimension reduction by PCA, thresholding method needs basic computation, and yields result close to PCA method.

articleTitle: Comparison Forecasting Methods for Electrical Energy Demand: In Case Study Luggage Manufacturing Industry
abstract: In the luggage manufacturing industry, electrical power demand is necessary for production and electricity cost, which can be predicted in advance for electricity usage and electricity demand, allowing for future production planning. This research presents a comparison of methods for forecasting electricity demand in the luggage manufacturing industry. The electricity consumption data from July 2020 to June 2024 is used to compare the forecasting methods of the decomposition method and simple exponential smoothing, which can effectively forecast using seasonal data and data fluctuations. It was found that factoring forecasting is more appropriate than simple exponential smoothing. When comparing the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) values of both methods, they are 1.37 and 2.39, respectively. The electric energy variable data has less error because it includes trend variables (T), seasonal variation (S), cyclical variation (C), and irregular variation (I). The factored forecast data, when used to forecast the electric energy demand for the 12-month period from July 2024 to June 2025, revealed a high electric energy value, necessitating the planning of future production. Therefore, forecasting electricity demand in the luggage manufacturing industry will help forecast and plan energy use more efficiently.

articleTitle: Smart Home Energy Management using BEVSE for Vehicle-to-Home (V2H) Systems
abstract: This paper presents a method for managing household energy consumption and production in homes utilizing electric vehicles (EVs). The approach integrates a Home Energy Management System (HEMS) with Bidirectional Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (BEVSE), which enables both charging and discharging of EVs using Vehicle-to-Home (V2H) and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technologies. These technologies allow EVs to supply power to household appliances and feed energy back into the grid while ensuring that energy consumption and distribution remain within the meter’s capacity limits. Simulation results from MATLAB Simulink demonstrate that this approach helps prevent potential damage to the power system, mitigates energy shortages, and enhances grid stability.

articleTitle: Automatic Crosswalk Detection and Counting Using YOLO and SAHI Techniques
abstract: The critical issue of pedestrian safety in large cities with high traffic density is focused on the effective detection and counting of pedestrians on crosswalks. This research proposes a deep learning model based on the You Only Look Once (YOLO) architecture, enhanced by the Slicing Aided Hyper Inference (SAHI) technique. The performance of several YOLO versions, including YOLOv8, YOLOv9, and YOLOv10, was evaluated with and without the integration of SAHI, using Accuracy, R-squared (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), and Mean Squared Error (MSE) as evaluation metrics. Our experimental results represent that, without SAHI, YOLOv9 achieved the highest accuracy of 37.52%, with an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value of 0.98 and an MSE of 19.36. When the SAHI technique was applied, YOLOv9+SAHI demonstrated a significant improvement by achieving an accuracy of 75.12%, maintaining an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value of 0.98, and reducing the MSE to 11.67. These findings highlight the effectiveness of SAHI in enhancing detection performance and reducing errors, particularly for YOLOv9, and improving the detection of small objects in complex environments. This study provides valuable insights into optimizing pedestrian detection systems, with YOLOv9 integrated with SAHI being the most effective model for pedestrian counting on crosswalks.

articleTitle: Light-Weight Gated Recurrent Unit for Electroencephalogram Emotion Classification
abstract: This experiment investigates the impact of reducing GRU units and dense layer neurons in a lightweight GRU architecture (LW-GRU-RU) compared to a baseline GRU model for electroencephalogram (EEG) emotion classification. A baseline GRU model is used as a reference, with an optimized GRU variant utilizing feature selection through a Random Forest-based algorithm. Experiments are conducted on a labeled emotion dataset, comparing accuracy and training efficiency across five trials. Results highlight the trade-off between model complexity, accuracy, and computational efficiency, providing insights for practical applications. Both models are evaluated on an emotion dataset for accuracy and training efficiency. The lightweight model achieves a competitive accuracy of 97.486% while reducing the average training time to 0.19 seconds per epoch, showcasing its potential for efficient real-world applications.

articleTitle: Single-Phase Single-Stage Bi-Directional H6 PEV Charger for V2H Application
abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) technology has become a leading trend in the future of transportation, widely recognized as a key strategy for reducing oil dependence, lowering greenhouse gas emissions, and enhancing energy conversion efficiency. In smart homes concept, the high-capacity batteries in EVs offer significant advantages as potential battery energy storage systems (BESS). EVs are expected to take on an active role in energy exchange with the home, enabled by bidirectional chargers. A major challenge for bi-directional chargers is achieving high power density. This research focuses on a transformerless topology as a promising solution to this challenge. This paper presents a single-phase, single-stage bidirectional H6 PEV charger designed for vehicle-to-home (V2H) applications. The proposed system operates in two modes: grid-to-vehicle (G2V) for charging and V2H for supplying power to the home. The design is based on a commercial single-phase 7.7 kVA PEV charger and has been validated through PSIM simulation.

articleTitle: Natural Language Processing for Subjective Exam Grading in Programming Explanations in Thai Language
abstract: In the digital era, learning programming has become an essential skill, and assessing students' understanding in this area plays a crucial role in enhancing educational quality. However, evaluating subjective programming exam responses, especially those involving conceptual explanations or procedural descriptions, remains a challenging task due to the diversity and complexity of answers. Manual grading can lead to delays and inconsistencies in scoring. This research aims to develop an automated system for evaluating Thai subjective programming exams using Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to assess the correctness of responses. The system is implemented in Python, utilizing the ThaiNLP library for word tokenization, alongside Machine Learning algorithms such as Naive Bayes, Decision Tree, and Support Vector Machine (SVM) for classification and prediction of answers. The experimental dataset includes responses from 120 students who answered subjective questions about Python commands. Expert testing indicated high user satisfaction with an average score of 4.05. The findings show that SVM achieved the highest accuracy at 85.33%. This system can enhance efficiency and consistency in exam evaluation, reducing grading time and contributing to standardized scoring.

articleTitle: Implementation of PV System for Reducing Village Common Expenses
abstract: This research demonstrates that implementing solar panels in housing estates can reduce some communal expenses, which are recurring financial burdens for residents. The research focuses on designing and simulating a solar energy system to supply electricity to the communal areas of a housing estate located in the Bangkok metropolitan area. The PVSyst software is primarily used to create models for analyzing the solar power generation system. Additionally, the research evaluates the system's feasibility through an economic analysis to determine its suitability for electricity.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Various Dual-Band AMC Structures Using Textile Materials
abstract: This paper presents the performance comparison of various dual-band AMC structures using textile materials. The textile AMC structure includes of the inner patch and outer loop to achieve dual-band operation. The felt is used as substrate of AMC unit cell while the copper-nickel plated polyester fabric is used as conductive parts. The various geometries of AMC unit cell based on square, circle, hexagon, octagon shapes are designed to operate at 2.4/5.5 GHz for WBAN and Wi-Fi applications. Moreover, the performance of AMC unit cell structures is compared in term of size and bandwidth. It is found from simulation results that the inner square patch and outer square loop can provide compact size and wider bandwidth. The hexagon shape can achieve compact size when it is arranged in form of array.

articleTitle: An inset-fed Patch Antenna with Corner Slots Designed for WLAN
abstract: The patch antenna with a slotted corner has a simple design and can be integrated into the printed circuit of the communication system. The design incorporates an inset feed with slots positioned at the top-left and top-right corners of the patch to enhance frequency response. Designed for WLAN applications, the antenna is implemented on a PCB with a dielectric constant of ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 4.7 and 1.6 mm of thickness. The voltage standing wave ratio is close to 1, and the return loss is less than -10 dB, providing a bandwidth of 130 MHz.

articleTitle: The Passenger Counting Prototype on the Aircraft Using Microwave Sensors
abstract: The prototype for an aircraft passenger counting system using microwave sensors is presented. The sensor was developed with a rectangular patch design using CST Microwave Studio software. Dimension 40 mm × 46 mm, the sensor is made of FR-4 material with a thickness of 1.6 mm and operates at a frequency of 2.4 GHz. A mock-up of an A310-200 aircraft door was constructed using PVC pipes. The dimensions of this simulated door are 80 cm× 230 cm. The passenger counting system was created using MATLAB, interfacing with a Nano-Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) to evaluate signal transmission and reflection properties. The sensor was mounted at a height of 80 cm, suitable for detecting children and aligning with the lower body of adults. Passengers of varying characteristics walked through the simulated door in three sessions, each with 50 participants. In the first two tests, 44 passengers were successfully counted, while the third test recorded 45 passengers. Overall, the sensor achieved an average accuracy of 88.33% in passenger counting.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Video Gain Equalizer via Distributed circuits
abstract: This paper presents a linear luminance and chrominance gain equalizer in video waveform transmission. Practically, the distributed devices have physical characteristics similar to the transmission line. Therefore, it can be employed to function in approximately as a passive lumped element. For this purpose, a novel transformation can be realized on equalizer using commemorated passive and active filters with uniformly distributed URC lines. In this paper we introduce two types of gain equalizers. The first type consists of resistive, conductive and capacitive, known as uniform GCR elements. The second type approximated by the uniformly distributed RC transfer function. As the results the proposed gain equalizer prove in equalizing both the luminance and chrominance gain distortions correction. From the simulation results, it is shown that the proposed distributed circuit gives good amplitude chrominance characteristic for both types of luminance gain equalizers.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on Feature Extraction for Battery State of Health Estimation: Evaluating the Role of Open Circuit Voltage in LSTM Model
abstract: This paper investigates the addition of the open circuit voltage (OCV) parameter for state of health (SOH) estimation using a long short-term memory (LSTM) model. The battery degradation data of Oxford University is used in the investigation. The variable used for training the models are charging and discharging currents and voltage, times and temperatures. The comparison shows that the model incorporating OCV data performs better in estimation accuracy than the model without OCV.

articleTitle: Design of an Electronically Controlled Biquadratic Filter Using Commercial ICs
abstract: This paper presents an electronically controlled biquadratic filter designed for precise frequency selection in applications such as audio processing, telecommunications, and cochlear implants. The design utilizes AD830, AD844, and LM13700 integrated circuits, facilitating high-pass, band-pass, and low-pass responses with improved stability and real-time tunability. PSPICE simulations validate the filter's adaptability and performance, demonstrating its effectiveness in dynamic environments and its suitability for high-frequency applications requiring flexible frequency control. The results indicate a calculated pole frequency of 2.23 MHz, while simulations yield a slightly lower value of 2.0 MHz, affirming the design's practical viability and alignment with theoretical expectations.

articleTitle: A Wideband Antenna Integrated into a Military Fabric for X-Band Satellite Communication
abstract: The study examines a wideband antenna solution that combines military fabric integration with X-band satellite functionality. The proposed antenna, with dimensions of 40×40×0.565 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, is constructed using gabardine fabric with a herringbone twill (HBT) pattern with physical parameters of 0.395 mm thickness, relative permittivity of 1.8848, and dielectric loss tangent measuring 0.02611. Testing in an anechoic chamber shows excellent agreement between simulated and measured results, with the antenna operating from 7.25 - 12.28 GHz, corresponding to a fractional bandwidth of 50.89%, a measured peak gain of 6.49 dBi, while radiation patterns, return loss, and gain measurements validate its practical performance. Exploiting advancements in wearable electromagnetic systems and demonstrating seamless integration into military apparel, the proposed antenna establishes a robust solution viable for deployment in sophisticated defense communication infrastructures.

articleTitle: An Efficient Repetitive Technique Based on Rank-Ordered Absolute Differences and Mean Filter for Suppressing Incidental-Magnitude Impulse Noise
abstract: In the noise suppressing surrounding, intensely Incidental-Magnitude Impulse Noise (IMIN), the regular noise suppressing technique, which is occasionally intermingled by the noise observing method and the noise filtering method, is an obligatory preprocessing technique that must be operated previous to the primary convoluted computer vision methods. Consequently, one of the practical and efficient noise observing method is the ROAD (Rank-Ordered-Absolute-Differences), which is proffered in 2008 for IMIN. Hence, this paper proffers the efficient repetitive technique, which is developed from the ordinary noise suppressing technique based on ROAD-AMF for IMIN, that is based on ROAD observing method with mean filter (MF) method under the repetitive framework. In the experimental section, various computer portrayals, which are intermingled of Lena, Girl and Baboon on wide IMIN density, are operated by the efficient repetitive technique (R-ROAD-MF) in comparability to anterior noise suppressing techniques: MF, SMF, AMF and ROAD-AMF. Because of these outstanding results, the efficient noise suppressing technique using R-ROAD-MF technique is more efficient than anterior noise suppressing techniques.

articleTitle: Construction and Verification of Small-Sized and Low Cut-Off Frequency Reverberant Chamber
abstract: Reverberant chambers are important in acoustical measurement due to their diffuseness in sound fields. However, design and construction of small reverberant chambers are challenging, since their cut-off frequencies are inversely proportional to their volume. This work is to design and construct a small-size reverberant chamber of not bigger than 3 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> volume, having low cut-off frequency not higher than 400 Hz. The design started with simulation so that the chamber shape can be adjusted to be irregular and complied with ISO standard. After construction of the chamber, performance evaluations of the chambers with four types of corner diffuser installation, were performed based on ISO 354 and ISO 3741 standards. Diffuseness of sound field in the chamber was verified using standard deviation of measured SPLs. After evaluation, it was found that the constructed reverberant chamber with the type-4 corner diffuser installation met the requirements for having a diffuse sound field at 400 Hz cut-off frequency. The chamber also has low background noise. The noise levels in frequency octave of 200 – 5000 Hz band were between 4-16 dB.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Same-Sense Circularly Polarized Grid-Metasurface Antenna for C-Band Spectrum Utilization
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-band circularly-polarized (CP) grid-metasurface (MTS) antenna for C-band frequencies. The proposed CP grid-MTS antenna comprised of upper, middle, and lower substrates. A 3 × 4 rotated H-shaped grid-MTS unit elements were located on upper substrate. A slot ground plane and feed line were positioned on middle and lower substrates, respectively. The H-shaped grid-MTS scheme can be converted linear-to-circular polarization. To achieve dual-band CP radiation, the Z-shaped slot and grid-MTS scheme rotation were applied to manipulate a return loss (RLBW) and axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW).
